articles.title: ‘I’m on the ticket’: Trump implores Republicans to vote in November at unusual midterm convention
articles.summary:
The president demonised Democrats in an attempt to wangle votes in midterms despite backlash over Iran war

With his approval rating at a historic low,

blocks.text: With his approval rating at a historic low, Donald Trump has brought down the curtain on the Republicans’ first ever midterm convention by pleading with supporters to do him “the biggest favour” and “pretend” they are voting for him in November’s US elections.

The president is facing a growing backlash over rising prices and the war in Iran. Sweeping losses for the Republican party could effectively turn Trump into a lame duck for his final two years in the White House.

Sensing political danger, Trump wrapped up the novel two-day event in Dallas, Texas, on Thursday with a pitch that critics are likely to say smacked of desperation: “You gotta do me the biggest favour you’ve ever done me. You’ve gotta do this for me. You’ve got to pretend I’m on the ticket. I’m on the ticket! I’m on the ticket! He’s on the ticket! Pretend I’m on the ticket because this is going to turn out to be one of the most important elections.”

In an improvised pledge of allegiance to himself, Trump directed the crowd of about 20,000 to raise their right hands and repeat: “I pledge to the greatest president in the history of the United States, that loves us so much he can’t even breathe, that I will go out with my family, my friends, I’ll do it any way – I don’t care if I’m registered or not, I’m going to try to cheat like hell like they do.”
The convention had been aimed at turning around Republicans’ fortunes. Opinion polls suggest they are on course to lose the US House of Representatives, and possibly the Senate.

In what was effectively an abridged version of his rambling keynote address on Wednesday, the president reiterated his promise of “Trump dividend” of $5,000 for every US adult if Republicans win both chambers of Congress. Democrats have dismissed the pledge as a bribe while economists have warned it would cost more than $1tn.
Trump also hammered the theme of the convention: drawing a contrast between his own accomplishments and what he argues amounts to a threat posed by Democrats.

“Less than two years ago, the American people gave us a mandate to save America – and in 19 months, I’ve delivered on every single promise I made,” he claimed. “They gave us wide open borders with 25 million people pouring in from all over the globe. They turned our cities into scenes of death and misery, murder, poverty and destruction, and made America a laughingstock all over world.
“But we took that dark age of America and turned it into the golden age of America.”

The reduction of prescription drug prices alone “should get us a big victory in our midterms”, he suggested, before he turned the microphone over to opera performer Christopher Macchio, who belted out a soaring rendition of America the Beautiful as red, white, blue and golden balloons cascaded down from the ceiling of the basketball arena.

The convention resembled a Trump mega-rally more than a traditional party meeting, with no nominations or formal business and more than 50 speakers or presentations each night. Supporters wore “Make America Great Again” regalia and waved signs displaying the Stars and Stripes. Republicans believe it has been successful in galvanising the party’s base in the face of stiff electoral headwinds.
Earlier on Thursday, speaker after speaker sought to champion Trump’s accomplishments while constantly branding the Democratic party as extremist and communist.
The president’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr, delivered a fiery address setting Republican “common sense” against a “dystopian hellscape” of leftwing ideology.

“As we speak, Democrat candidates across the country are openly embracing the radical ideology of democratic socialism,” suggested Trump Jr. “They claim that their socialism is for the people, but that’s the exact same story we’ve heard from every communist in human history.”
Describing childhood memories of his grandparents in communist Czechoslovakia, he warned of bread lines and rationing. “Communism is on the march and it’s up to us to stop it in its tracks,” he said.

Trump Jr framed the Republican platform, including pledges to end taxes on tips, overtime and social security, as a direct response to a “war on the working people” by Democrats. “The choice is clear,” he said. “Don’t let these radicals gaslight you into thinking common sense is extreme, and extreme is somehow common sense. Don’t let them convince you that caring about this country makes you a villain.”
after newsletter promotion

Senator Ted Cruz meanwhile warned of a “red-green alliance” between “communists and Islamists” who “hate Christians, hate Jews and hate capitalism”. Invoking his father’s escape from Cuban communism, Cruz declared that “sharia law has no place in America” and is “fundamentally inconsistent with the constitution”.

The House speaker, Mike Johnson, echoed the conspiratorial tone, suggesting the nation was being “attacked from within”. The Democratic party is now beholden to radicals, he claimed, warning: “They’re the ones who have let the barbarians inside the gate, and next year the communists will be in Congress. That’s what’s so frightening.”

Johnson added that, while big names like Zohran Mamdani and Abdul El-Sayed are known entities, the bigger threat comes from “Democrats in the swing seats who say one thing, and then join forces and vote with the socialists that they’re afraid of”.

The US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, took the stage to champion the “Make America Healthy Again” (Maha) platform. The son of a former US attorney general and nephew of John F Kennedy said the “irony of my presence here is inescapable”.

He continued: “The Democrats of that era stood with labour and working people and the American middle class. Nearly every cop and firefighter was a Democrat … The Democratic party, in short, lost its way.”

Speaking less than a mile from the spot where his uncle was assassinated in 1963, Kennedy claimed it was a “fact” that “neither my father, nor my uncle, would recognise the Democratic party of today”.

JD Vance, the vice-president, gave the keynote address of the night. He said: “The Democrats are the party of hatred. They’re the party that despises America and the people who built it … America belongs to those who love it – not those who hate it.”
The political attacks were briefly paused for two sombre interludes.

A tribute marked one year since the assassination of rightwing provocateur and organiser Charlie Kirk. Lucas Miles, a Turning Point USA vice-president, said that while “they could take the man, they could not take the mission”. Chants of “Charlie, Charlie” filled the air.

The arena was plunged into darkness as Macchio performed Ave Maria on the eve of the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks. Two beams of light stretched upward from the arena floor, reminiscent of the twin towers in New York, as the crowd held up mobile phone lights. A video narration accompanying the tribute urged the audience to: “Say their names. Honour their sacrifice. Defend Freedom. Never forget September 11.”

Democrats have dismissed the Republican event as a stunt. At a press conference in Dallas, the congressman Robert Garcia, of California, told reporters: “What’s happening right now is Donald Trump is throwing a two-day party to celebrate himself, so that JD Vance can give a speech, and so his donors, some of whom have paid $800,000 a pop for these ticket packages, can spend two days celebrating themselves.

“This is happening as the American public is struggling. So as Donald Trump and JD Vance party away for two days, the average American family can’t afford groceries, the cost of the rent’s going up, they’re looking at their gas prices skyrocketing and they’re making difficult choices at the dinner table. But Donald Trump does not care about the average American family or about affordability.”

articles.summary: Zeshan Hamdani, who lost his older brother in the North Tower, is speaking out after push back against New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani attending the 25-year memorial.

blocks.text: This year’s 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks has become embroiled in divisive politics. There are controversial calls for the city’s first Muslim Mayor to sit out the commemorative event, including from Rudy Giuliani who was New York’s mayor on the morning of 9/11.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani has said he will attend and his focus will be on the families who lost loved ones.
Zeshan Hamdani lost his older brother Salman, a Muslim American New York police cadet, in the North Tower. He spoke to the BBC's Nada Tawfik over his thoughts on this anniversary.

articles.title: $15m fund launched to create ‘unstoppable momentum’ to end FGM worldwide
articles.summary:
Her Horizon Fund seeks $100m to stop practice harming 230m women and girls globally

Frontline activists and leaders in the fight against female genital mutilation, which has affected more…

blocks.text: Frontline activists and leaders in the fight against female genital mutilation, which has affected more than 230 million women and girls worldwide, have welcomed an unprecedented $15.5m (£11.4m) fund aimed at creating “unstoppable momentum” to finally end the practice.

The launch of the fund comes as women’s rights are increasingly under attack and donor funding is in sharp decline, particularly for work led by FGM survivors in local communities. It is thought to be the largest single philanthropic contribution to ending the practice of FGM.
The United Nations has set a goal of elimination by by 2030, but progress is not on track as funding declines and legal protections are challenged.

Funding received by the largest initiative to end the practice – a joint programme operated in 18 countries by the UN’s sexual and reproductive health agency, UNFPA, and the UN humanitarian organisation for children, Unicef – fell by 45% last year, from $29.6m to $16.3m.
The Her Horizon Fund has been seeded with $14m from the Wallace Global Fund, plus an additional $1.5m contribution from an anonymous donor, making $15.5m in total.
The aim of Her Horizon Fund, set up by the US-based Wallace Global Fund, is to pool $100m from donors to reach a “tipping point” towards ending FGM within a generation.

Ifrah Ahmed, a Somali-Irish activist and survivor of FGM who set up the Ifrah Foundation to end practice in Somalia, where it is nearly universal, said: “By giving $14m, the global fund will ensure activists can continue their work in this area.”

UN funding worth $300,000 to her organisation was cut by UNFPA last year, but Ahmed managed to raise money from elsewhere. The Ifrah Foundation has helped push for anti-FGM legislation in Somalia, she said.

Three of Somalia’s seven federal member states have enacted anti-FGM laws, while in two other states bills banning the practice have been endorsed by cabinet and are awaiting parliamentary approval, albeit with opposition by religious leaders in some areas.
“If we don’t continue to raise money, the dream where this practice will end will have died for young girls,” she added.

Advocates warn that while international recognition of FGM as a human rights violation has grown, and countries such as Burkina Faso, the Gambia and Kenya have criminalised the practice, progress remains fragile.
In recent years, survivors and frontline groups have been trying to protect gains made over several decades.

The Gambia’s supreme court, for instance, is considering a constitutional challenge to the country’s 2015 ban on female genital mutilation and cutting. The case follows a 2024 parliamentary effort to repeal the ban, which lawmakers rejected after months of debate, amid strong resistance from women’s rights groups. In Sierra Leone, the new Child Rights Act does not prohibit FGM, despite sustained campaigning from rights groups.

Susan Gibbs, the Wallace Global Fund’s senior adviser on women’s rights and FGM, said: “Female genital mutilation is a global crisis, an extreme manifestation of gender-based violence and violence against children, and a public health emergency.

“There has been decades of progress, and UN data indicates declines in prevalence in a number of countries. But there have also been anti-rights pushback and political crises. Obviously, donor funding is in decline. So it’s a mixed picture.”
after newsletter promotion

She added: “We’re at this critical inflection point. Most frontline organisations have been absolutely starved for resources, and so more direct funding would allow them to sustain and scale [up] their work.”
Gibbs, who attended a Justice for Girls global gathering in Kenya earlier this month, where the fund was officially launched, said the momentum at the meeting was “incredible”.

“Lasting change must be led by the frontline – it cannot be imposed from the outside. Frontline survivors, activists, they know their communities and they know what it will take. They must have the resources and power to lead.
“I’m convinced the impact [of the fund] will be catalytic,” she said. “There’s no doubt in my mind that with adequate funding, these frontline activists have what it takes to get this done.”

FGM is the partial or total removal of female genitalia for non-medical reasons. It has been endured by more than 144 million women and girls in Africa, 80 million in Asia and 6 million in the Middle East. The practice can cause immediate health complications such as severe pain, excessive bleeding and infection, as well as long-term consequences that include complications during childbirth, chronic pain and lasting psychological trauma.
A 2025 study estimated that FGM causes approximately 44,000 deaths each year in the 15 countries examined, making it one of the leading causes of death for women and girls in those countries.

articles.title: Customers of UK-owned surrogacy firm in Mexico allegedly face huge bills after insurance denied
articles.summary:
UK government reviewing allegations about My Surrogacy Journey after complaints about medical costs

The UK government has said it is reviewing allegations about a British-owned surrogacy…

blocks.text: The UK government has said it is reviewing allegations about a British-owned surrogacy service after surrogates in Mexico who faced health complications including a hysterectomy had their insurance claims rejected.

The Department of Health and Social Care is considering whether the UK-based provider My Surrogacy Journey should remain listed on gov.uk as one of four domestic surrogacy agencies available to intended parents, after its Mexican sister company received complaints.

Emails sent by the chief executive of My Surrogacy Journey seen by the Guardian suggest multiple surrogate women had their insurance claims rejected in Mexico, where the surrogates are based. The emails suggest 300 couples going through a “surrogacy journey” with the company have been moved to a new insurance provider due to the increased risk of claims being rejected.

In the UK, commercial surrogacy is banned and only altruistic surrogacy arrangements are permitted. My Surrogacy Journey has a UK branch which is not-for-profit, and also has for-profit sister companies operating in Mexico and the US, where commercial surrogacy is legal in some states. All three companies have the same owners and chief executives. It is My Surrogacy Journey’s Mexico-based surrogacies which have had insurance issues.
One couple the Guardian spoke to said they paid tens of thousands of pounds to cover the medical costs of their surrogate who had a hysterectomy during birth after her insurance claim was refused.
My Surrogacy Journey was founded in 2021 by the couple Michael and Wes Johnson-Ellis, both from Birmingham, who set it up after having their own children via surrogacy.

The couple, now based in the Cayman Islands, say their company is a “UK surrogacy organisation like no other” with “one of the most enviable advisory boards for a surrogacy not-for-profit organisation” and that it is the “new face of surrogacy”.
The Guardian understands at least five sets of parents say they had to foot the bill for medical costs after insurance claims were refused.

An email seen by the Guardian sent by Michael Johnson-Ellis to the couple whose surrogate had a hysterectomy said: “We have already told you that the insurance companies have been declining some of the claims and we are actively working with the broker to get this issue resolved but you should also consider that they may not be paid out and there is nothing we are able to do to change this ... We appreciate this is not an insignificant sum but this genuinely is out of our control.”
Johnson-Ellis added in the email that the company had switched to a new insurance provider, explaining: “We’re also managing this for 300 other journeys, which is a complex position to be in.”

Lawyers acting for My Surrogacy Journey said the company did not comment on individual cases, but that existing insurance policies were in place and claims continued to be accepted and processed. They said the company was of the understanding that a small number of claims were rejected and was supporting those seeking to resolve claims with an insurer.
It is understood that as part of the surrogacy arrangement intended parents are contractually required to cover any medical costs that may not be covered by an insurer.

The couple who spoke to the Guardian reported being recommended to take the “Mexico option”. The website advertises that those who go to Mexico can have a baby in “under 18 months”. The parents say they were told the UK option can take up to five years, and that the US route is much more expensive. Lawyers acting for My Surrogacy Journey said that intended or prospective parents were provided with information about what the surrogacy process entails, including typical timelines, cost, legal frameworks and practical considerations in a transparent and understandable way, and that the 18-month period is indicative only.
after newsletter promotion

The couple described their dream of having a baby turning into a nightmare when their surrogate developed a serious condition known as placenta accreta, which is when the placenta attaches to the wall of the uterus.

The emails from Johnson-Ellis acknowledge that the insurance provider investigated the birth after the woman’s health complications. One email reads: “As your surrogate’s care took an unexpected turn, this later led to even more scrutiny by the hospital and insurance provider – which we have no control over.”
The parents are considering legal action, and the Guardian understands at least four other couples are reviewing their options.

Phil Brickell, the MP for Bolton West, raised the concerns of a separate couple who had used My Surrogacy Journey. He told parliament during a debate regarding surrogacy on Monday: “Two of my constituents recently travelled to Mexico, where their children were born by surrogacy. Those births were facilitated by a company called My Surrogacy Journey, which is listed on gov.uk. While in Mexico, they had repeated traumatic experiences with the company relating to issues including insurance for their children, accusations of bullying towards staff and repeated efforts to silence any constructive criticism. I understand that other members of this house have received similar complaints.”
Brickell is calling for the government to “take My Surrogacy Journey down from gov.uk pending a review by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority”.

The health minister Diana Johnson said the government was reviewing allegations made regarding My Surrogacy Journey. She said: “The department is looking into the allegations about My Surrogacy Journey. As part of that assessment, the department will consider whether it is appropriate for that company to remain on the gov.uk list of agencies”. A DHSC spokesperson confirmed to the Guardian that the government was reviewing allegations about My Surrogacy Journey. Lawyers acting for My Surrogacy Journey said the company was in communication with DHSC and it was confident any issues could be resolved.

Dr Bianca Jackson, a surrogacy law expert at Coram Chambers, said the case highlighted by the Guardian seemed “incredibly worrying”. She said: “For the past 13 years, I have acted for intended parents applying for parental orders for children born in many different countries. Though I have come across a plethora of issues with agencies abroad, I have never come across this problem in practice. My experience suggests that this is not a wide or prevalent issue with surrogacy abroad and it is limited to Mexico/the organisation you are investigating, but it is still incredibly worrying.”

The London-based surrogacy consultant Shaun Thomas, who founded The Surrogacy Father after his own experience having children via surrogate, said insurance could get “very complicated”, especially when it involved third-party reproduction like IVF and navigating healthcare systems abroad.

He said intended parents needed to make sure their insurance covered both the surrogate and the baby, adding that some policies did not always include neonatal intensive care unit admission or may exclude certain hospitals.
Lawyers acting for My Surrogacy Journey said the health and wellbeing of surrogates and babies as well as that of intended parents was at the core of its values.

articles.title: Reform UK beset by internal row over response to Dover and Portsmouth protests
articles.summary:
Nigel Farage said demonstrators in balaclavas were ‘horrible’, but others in the party defend them as ‘brave, passionate patriots’

Nigel Farage’s condemnation of the masked men whose…

blocks.text: Nigel Farage’s condemnation of the masked men whose blockade of Dover stole headlines on the final day of his party’s annual conference was swift, describing their actions as “horrible”.

Yet less than a week on from the public debut of the black-clad members of Patriot Platform, Reform is gripped with internal friction over the activists. There has been unease among some members and councillors about Farage’s criticism and some outright praise for the group as “patriots”.

Reform is facing questions about explicit links to the nationalist hard right after Ryan Bridge, a co-founder of the anti-migrant Raise the Colours group, was given a prominent platform at Reform’s conference, where Farage pledged to “legally back” him.

Bridge, who was on bail and was charged this week with 14 offences including racially aggravated harassment, has worked closely with the leader of Patriot Platform, Daniel Thomas. Bridge has said he has no association with Patriot Platform.
The starkest public example of Reform divisions over Patriot Platform played out publicly in Portsmouth on Monday after police had clashed with activists wearing balaclavas.

Thomas gatecrashed a visit by the party’s home affairs spokesperson, Zia Yusuf, to tell him that events had been misreported. “I take your word for it,” Yusuf told him. Yusuf later reflected that Thomas – a convicted criminal and long-term associate of the activist who calls himself Tommy Robinson – made his points “respectfully” and challenged Kemi Badenoch’s condemnation of the group. “How dare you call them ‘thugs’,” Yusuf told the Conservative leader on X.

blocks.caption: The Patriot Platform founder Daniel Thomas, left, speaks to the Reform UK home affairs spokesperson, Zia Yusuf, in Portsmouth on Monday. Photograph: Theo Shaw/PA

blocks.text: Yusuf and other senior Reform figures including Richard Tice, Robert Jenrick and the leader of the party’s flagship county council, Kent, have criticised the use of face coverings by the new far-right group. But often in the same breath there has been tacit backing for their aims.

“How about your government stops the boats instead? Then people wouldn’t feel the need to protest over the invasion of the country … just a thought,” said the Kent council leader, Linden Kemkaran, whose council includes Dover.
Yet elsewhere – as highlighted by the anti-fascist group Hope Not Hate – others have been willing to go further.

“Those patriots in Portsmouth have done more to stop the invasion than the last seven governments put together,” said the Dudley councillor Andrew Southall, while the Portsmouth councillor Emily Strudwick spoke of “a great sense of community” at the protest, which she attended.
There is also, unusually, evidence of open dissent in Reform towards Farage himself.

“We know there are strong feelings circulating today about Nigel’s comments regarding the Dover protest. We want to address it head on as a group,” the Tameside councillor Sharon Barker wrote on Facebook.

“Many of the people at that march were brave, passionate patriots who had very real reasons for covering their faces, including the very real fear of losing their jobs simply for standing up for Britain.”

blocks.caption: Masked protesters march in Dover

blocks.text: Her group leader, Allan Hopwood, told the Guardian that the subject was “particularly emotive”, insisting the focus was on democratic politics. A factor in Tameside is that Reform locally is at the sharp end of the threat posed by the rightwing rival Rupert Lowe’s Restore Britain.

But on the question of face coverings worn by the activists, Hopwood said: “These are people who clearly have a patriotic agenda and are concerned about the women and children of this country, but they are also acutely aware there will be media who want to propagandise things. They will have jobs they want to protect and unfortunately we’re in a position where people are reluctant to make their identities known.”

During the Reform conference, Farage told Bridge of Raise the Colours that its campaign – which put up flags around England in circumstances that many people saw as intimidating – had been “phenomenal” and he would pass the group’s proposal to partner with Reform-led councils on to the party’s lawyers, an exchange that has been shared widely on social media.

Bridge told the Guardian on Thursday that he had received a lot of interest from Reform councillors about his proposal and the party was considering the plans. “Specific councils are in acknowledgment of what we are trying to roll out and propose. It’s very, very positive from Clacton to Norfolk to Wales. Last night, I spoke to councillors in Burnley, it’s literally the whole country,” he said.
“It felt like we were in a comfortable, safe environment of like-minded British patriots and people that want better for the country,” he said.

The praise for Patriot Platform among some in Reform and ties to Raise the Colours come at a perilous moment for Farage as he seeks to nudge up Reform’s flatlining poll numbers by tempting wavering Tory voters.

While he is fond of laying claim to being the man who killed off the British National party when it was competing with Ukip a decade ago, Reform faces an acute electoral danger of losing voters on its right to Restore Britain.
Reform UK was approached for comment.

articles.title: Resil Mojares honored with Day of National Mourning on September 12
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — September 12, 2026, has been declared a Day of National Mourning following the death of National Artist for Literature Resil B. Mojares, who passed away on September 5, a day…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — September 12, 2026, has been declared a Day of National Mourning following the death of National Artist for Literature Resil B. Mojares, who passed away on September 5, a day after his 83rd birthday.

Under Proclamation No. 1434, signed on September 10 by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto by the authority of President Ferdinand R. Marcos, the country will honor Mojares for his invaluable contributions to Philippine literature, cultural studies, regional history, and the formation of Cebuano and national identity.
Palace honors Mojares’ contributions

In the proclamation, Malacañang cited Mojares’ works and achievements as a teacher, scholar, essayist, fictionist, and historian, noting his vital role in championing regional scholarship and national culture.
Mojares was declared a National Artist under Proclamation No. 606, series of 2018, in recognition of his body of work and achievements.
The Palace said his passing is a great loss to the Filipino people and to the country’s cultural and artistic community.

It also recognized Mojares as a pivotal figure in Philippine literature and cultural studies, saying his contributions significantly enriched the nation’s understanding and appreciation of its literary and cultural heritage.
Flag to fly at half-mast
As part of the national mourning, the proclamation directs that the Philippine flag be flown at half-mast from sunrise to sunset on September 12.
The directive covers all government buildings and installations throughout the Philippines and abroad.

The proclamation cited Section 27(k), Chapter 1 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 8491, or the Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines, in relation to Proclamation No. 1001, series of 1972, as amended, as the basis for the half-mast directive.
The proclamation also said the nation mourns and joins Mojares’ family and friends in the period of grief and remembrance.
Thus, September 12 will serve as a nationwide observance honoring Mojares and recognizing his contributions to Philippine literary and cultural heritage.

articles.title: JD Vance pitches himself as Trump’s political heir on day two of Republican midterm convention
articles.summary:
Vice-president dog-whistled, exaggerated claims of success and echoed Trump talking points to excited audience

JD Vance made a clear pitch that he should be the heir to

blocks.text: JD Vance made a clear pitch that he should be the heir to Donald Trump on Thursday night, closing out the Republicans’ midterm convention with a blistering speech that featured exaggerated claims of success, criticism of Democrats as “lunatics” and an aggressive dismissal of a protester waving a Mexican flag.

Speaking in Dallas, the vice-president showed he could channel the basest instincts of his boss, filling his remarks with dog whistles and echoing Trump’s false claims that Democrats “cheered” the 7 October massacre of Israelis.

Vance had been met with chants of “JD, JD,” as he walked on to the stage: the liveliest response anyone besides Trump received across the two-day convention, with some shouting that he should be the nominee in 2028.
“We gotta take care of business this November, then we’ll worry about what comes next,” the vice-president responded with a smile.

Vance began the speech by running through a list of Republican grievances, channeling Trump’s pugnacious attitude toward immigration as he told the crowd that two years ago “we were tired of being called racist for noticing that our country was becoming dirtier and poorer and less safe and less prosperous”.

The Make America Great Again (Maga) crowd inside the arena liked that line, but the loudest cheer of the night came when Vance responded to a protester who briefly interrupted his speech. Vance claimed the protester was waving a Mexican flag, and adopted a fiery tone as he said: “Well, my friend, if you love Mexico so much, get your ass over there I’ll buy you the plane ticket.”
The applause was rapturous.

The vice-president had to walk a tightrope coming into the speech, arguably the most important address of his short political career. He had to present his own case to the Republican base, without breaking too much from the notoriously sensitive Trump.
Vance praised Trump as “the toughest SOB in American politics”, and paused repeatedly as the crowd lavished him with cheers and applause.
He also invoked the recent birth of fourth child, saying he had been looking at “the future of this country through the eyes of the future of my son” and “the birthright of this newest of Americans”.
Addressing Democratic “radicals”, whom he accused of wanting to destroy the nuclear American family, he boomed: “Stay the hell away from our kids.”

But it was also a speech aimed squarely at rallying the Maga faithful: attacking transgender rights, extolling the importance of American manufacturing and religious freedom, and accusing Democrats of “doubling down on the crazy”.

Vance showed a penchant, too, for Trump’s baseless statements, claiming that some Democrats in New York “cheered on” the slaughter of Jewish people on 7 October, and suggesting that a “new generation” of Democrats seek to defund the police and “abolish the border”.

“What is it that drives this new generation of radical Democrats? It’s not new policies. They’ll say the same stuff: defund the police, abolish the border, the green new scam. We’ve heard all this stuff before,” Vance said. He then tried out a new line: “I think that what’s new about them is what motivates them is a new type of hardcore hatred.”

Vance won applause, too, for his praise of Charlie Kirk, the far-right activist who was assassinated in Utah exactly one year ago. Addressing Kirk’s children, who were not in the arena, Vance said: “History will record that your father was a great man.

“Those of us who loved your dad, we know him as something even better than a great man – he was a good man,” he added of Kirk, a man who, among other things, endorsed Trump’s stolen-election lies and the racist great replacement theory.
after newsletter promotion

One problem Vance could face should he run in 2028 is his attachment to the deeply unpopular Iran war, and foreign policy was conspicuous by its absence in his speech. Last week he rejected the use of the word “war”, but said he wouldn’t set “artificial lines” regarding an end to the conflict. The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Trump’s advisers have raised the prospect that the war could drag on through the rest of his term.
Vance did not address the war directly. But in an oblique reference he invoked Kirk’s disdain for conflict.
“Charlie hated war,” Vance said, before pleading with undecided voters to not abandon the party over policy differences.

“What I’m asking you to do is do what Charlie did: do not throw the baby out with the bathwater,” he said. “Don’t don’t give the country over to a bunch of crazy people because you happen to disagree with us on a policy issue here or there.”

A poll found Vance was the favorite choice among likely Republican primary voters, with 43% saying they wanted him to be the nominee in 2028. Marco Rubio, the secretary of state, got 21%; Donald Trump Jr was at 7%.

Vance will hope those numbers stick, but he wasn’t the only one auditioning in Dallas. Robert F Kennedy Jr, the health secretary who switched parties to support Trump in 2024, praised the president and attacked the Democratic party during a well-received speech earlier on Thursday, while Ted Cruz, the Texas senator, received a rousing response in his home state.

“They hate Christians, they hate Jews, they hate the ‌capitalism, they hate ⁠the constitution and they hate America,” Cruz said of Democrats, offering no evidence for his claims, but very much tapping into the theme of the two-day convention.

Rubio did not speak at the convention, instead taking part in a tour of South America. Both he and Cruz ran against Trump in 2016. During that contest, Trump dubbed Rubio “Little Marco” and suggested Cruz’s father was involved in the assassination of John F Kennedy.

Vance, by contrast, has never publicly attracted Trump’s ire, and he will want to keep it that way as he seeks to take on leadership of the party in two years’ time. That was likely the thinking as the vice-president ended his speech, shouting over jubilant applause that Trump was the “greatest president” before relinquishing the stage for his boss to bring the convention to a close.

articles.title: Sara Duterte calls on Marcos to resign: 'Wala siyang utang na loob sa taumbayan'
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday called on President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. to step down from office during a rally at the Quezon City Hall following her rescheduled arraignment in…

blocks.text: Published September 11, 2026 11:43am

Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday called on President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. to step down from office during a rally at the Quezon City Hall following her rescheduled arraignment in relation to her grave threats case.
"Patuloy tayong manawagan ng paglayas ng problema ng ating bayan na ang pangalan ay Bongbong Marcos. Resign! Umalis ka dyan!" Duterte told her supporters.
(Let us continue to clamor that our nation's problem would leave. The name of that problem is Bongbong Marcos. Resign! Leave!)

"Sinungaling ka, abusado ka, wala siyang utang na loob sa taumbayan. Wala siyang utang na loob sa lahat ng pumunta ng presinto para iluklok siya sa pwesto. Wala siyang hiya. Ganoon talaga kapag adik. Hindi na dumadaan sa realidad ang pag-iisip. Patuloy tayong makipaglaban sa mga abusado, sa mga adik, at sa mga korap," she added.

(You're a liar, abusive. He has no debt of gratitude to our people and everyone who went to the precincts to put him in power. He has no shame. That's how it is with addicts. Their thoughts are not grounded on reality. Let us continue to fight the abusive ones, the addicts, and the corrupt.)
Duterte made the statement after attending her arraignment at Quezon City Hall of Justice for grave threat charges, which was postponed due to a motion filed by her camp.
GMA News Online has requested comment from Malacañang regarding Duterte's threat, but it has yet to respond as of posting time.
Marcos is scheduled to attend the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India from September 12 to 13.
The Department of Justice on August 11 filed grave threats charges against Duterte in connection with remarks she made in an online press conference in 2024.
Duterte said she already spoke with someone to kill Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and then House speaker Martin Romualdez if anything happened to her.
Her alleged threat is the basis of one of four Articles of Impeachment she is currently facing before the Senate impeachment court. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Bookmark this page for Rappler's comprehensive coverage of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

articles.title: Hurricane Lowell knocks out key Hawaii port, disrupting food, fuel
articles.summary: HONOLULU — Crews began repairing the only cargo port on one of Hawaii’s smallest main islands while power was being restored to another island Thursday, two days after Hurricane Lowell skirted…

blocks.text: HONOLULU — Crews began repairing the only cargo port on one of Hawaii’s smallest main islands while power was being restored to another island Thursday, two days after Hurricane Lowell skirted along the state’s western edge. At least two deaths were linked to the storm.

On the island of Kauai, intense wind and surging waves damaged oceanfront resorts, ripped apart roads and knocked out power, prompting tourism officials to urge visitors to stay away for now. On Lanai, a harbor that supplies much of the food and fuel to its 3,300 residents was inoperable and will take about two weeks to repair, state officials said.

The overall destruction to Hawaii’s infrastructure, businesses and homes was expected to be the worst from a storm since Hurricane Iniki, a Category 4 storm that walloped Kauai in 1992 and caused $3 billion in damage.

While it has been a relatively quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there have been four hurricanes in the Pacific since the beginning of August. Another tropical storm formed Thursday, but it was not expected to make landfall.
Tourism takes a hit

Officials urged travelers to reschedule trips to Kauai or shift their destination to another island. Thousands of customers, including some resorts, remained without power, and crews continued clearing roads of downed trees and toppled utility poles.

“Adjusting your itinerary allows you to continue your Hawaiʻi vacation while supporting the state’s broader visitor economy as Kauaʻi recovers,” Caroline Anderson, interim president and chief executive officer of the Hawai‘i Tourism Authority, said in a statement.

Kauai sees only a small fraction of Hawaii’s almost 10 million visitors each year, but tourism is its top economic driver, with people coming from all over to take in its tropical landscapes, waterfalls and dramatic cliffs. Local estimates say tourism accounts for 4 out of every 10 jobs on the island.

The hurricane’s powerful storm surge buckled and washed away roads, knocked down the walls of homes and flooded resorts, sending rapids through a hotel lobby, overturning furniture and leaving debris everywhere. Extensive lines backed up at Kauai’s primary airport Thursday as people tried to depart the island.
Despite running a restaurant business, Kelly Kakalia, co-owner of The Musubi Truck, with three locations across Kauai, said she is not overly worried about the interruption to tourism.
“I would be silly to say tourism doesn’t drive our economy,” she said, but “our island needs time to rest and rebuild and make sure locals have power and water” before welcoming back tourists.
“If we take a little hit, that’s just part of it,” Kakalia said.
Governor asks Trump to declare a disaster
Democratic Gov. Joshn Green asked President Donald Trump on Wednesday to issue a major disaster declaration to expedite federal help for Kauai and Maui counties.
“We cannot wait for every damaged road, utility pole, harbor and public facility to be assigned a dollar value before asking the federal government to act,” Green said in making the request.
At Lanai’s main harbor, the storm opened a sinkhole, damaged part of the pier and scattered containers in the water, according to the state’s Transportation Department.

Planning was underway on other options to get supplies to the island, which sees only a few visitors. Billionaire Larry Ellison bought nearly all of the island in 2012 for about $300 million from the owner of agriculture and real estate company Castle & Cooke Inc.
First responders on Kauai’s south end found the body of a 74-year-old man Wednesday near the shoreline. Authorities believe his death was related to the storm surge, police said.
Another man was killed on Oahu when a large tree fell on his tent Monday during the storm, the governor said. The man was homeless and living in a park./dp

articles.summary: Anthropic says cybercriminals and state-backed hackers were increasingly using AI not just to assist with tasks but to orchestrate and execute large portions of cyberattacks

blocks.text: ANTHROPIC. The Anthropic logo is seen in this illustration taken June 11, 2026.
Dado Ruvic/Reuters
Anthropic says cybercriminals and state-backed hackers were increasingly using AI not just to assist with tasks but to orchestrate and execute large portions of cyberattacks

items: Anthropic reported disrupting several malicious uses of its Claude models, including a suspected Russia-linked cyber espionage campaign and efforts by Chinese firms to replicate Claude's capabilities.

The company identified increased use of AI by cybercriminals and state-backed hackers to orchestrate cyberattacks, with notable incidents involving Chinese labs and the Russian hacking group Midnight Blizzard.
Anthropic highlighted new categories of threat actors misusing AI for developing software related to conventional weapons and detected activities linked to the ShinyHunters cybercrime collective.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Anthropic on Thursday, September 10, said it had disrupted several allegedly malicious uses of its Claude models over the past eight months, including a suspected Russia-linked cyber espionage campaign and efforts by Chinese AI firms it accused of trying to extract and replicate Claude’s capabilities.

Cybercriminals and state-backed hackers were increasingly using AI not just to assist with tasks but to orchestrate and execute large portions of cyberattacks, Anthropic said in its latest Threat Intelligence report. It added that humans were often overseers rather than hands-on operators.
“The use of AI went beyond simple questions and responses from a chatbot but rather involved the use of multi-agent frameworks executing” tasks, Anthropic said.
Anthropic said it had disrupted attacks from seven China-based labs during that period. Among the labs Anthropic named were tech giant Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek, and Xiaomi.

Operators it linked to Alibaba ran what Anthropic called the largest “illicit distillation” attack, allegedly aimed at extracting capabilities of Claude models and using them to improve the Chinese tech firm’s Qwen models, the company said. Alibaba did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Anthropic said it observed more than 151 million exchanges it attributed to Alibaba between May and July 2026, peaking at nearly 3 million per day from more than 3,500 accounts it described as fraudulent.
Distillation refers to the process of training smaller AI models using output from larger, more expensive models in a bid to lower the costs of training a new AI tool.

Rather than running bulk queries, Kimi chatbot creator Moonshot and DeepSeek allegedly routed live customer conversations, which sometimes included sensitive information, through Claude and used its responses as training data, Anthropic alleged.

A hacking group whose tradecraft was consistent with Russia-based threat actor Midnight Blizzard allegedly ran phishing, hotel Wi-Fi hijacking and WhatsApp-takeover operations against targets in the Ukrainian government, military and diplomatic sectors, using AI at nearly every stage, Anthropic said.

The US government has previously linked Midnight Blizzard, a tracking term coined by Microsoft, to Russia’s SVR foreign intelligence service. The Russian Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The group allegedly used AI to build a system that automatically detected when its malware was flagged by security defenses and rewrote the code until it evaded detection again.

Anthropic also identified what it called “new categories of threat actors” misusing Claude, including those using the platform to “develop software for conventional weapons, including firearms, missiles, armed drones, bombs, and other munitions, as well as the targeting and control systems that operate them.” The report detailed incidents of operators using Claude to develop software for weapons design and development, or to support intelligence gathering and procurement related to weapons programs, in China, Russia, and Yemen.

The company said that it detected and disrupted activity linked to affiliates of the ShinyHunters cybercrime collective, one of the most prolific cybercrime enterprises in recent months linked to attacks on major corporations around the world.

Jacob Klein, head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, said in an interview that models have become more capable over the last year, raising new risks. “A year ago, let’s say you wanted to optimize a drone or optimize the software on a missile, the models just wouldn’t be as good at that task as they are now,” he said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: COA finds irregularities in TUPAD payouts in 2025
articles.summary: State auditors spot issues in TUPAD payouts in Eastern Visayas, Davao Region, Soccskargen, and Caraga

blocks.text: State auditors spot issues in TUPAD payouts in Eastern Visayas, Davao Region, Soccskargen, and Caraga

MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Audit (COA) has found that thousands of Department of Labor and Employment’s (DOLE) Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD) beneficiaries in 2025 either received cash assistance despite submitting incomplete documents or got excess cash assistance.

State auditors said 2,731 beneficiaries were still paid even though they failed to comply with the eligibility documents set under Section 8 of Department Order No. 239, Series of 2023, including submission of valid government-issued ID cards.
Among the areas where these cases were found were:

items: Eastern Visayas Region with 1,093 beneficiaries
Davao Region with 1,091 beneficiaries
Soccskargen with 523 beneficiaries
Caraga Region with 24 beneficiaries

blocks.text: Auditors also said 2,781 senior citizens received TUPAD funds even though the medical certificates they submitted did not come from a licensed physician.
The questionable payouts cost the DOLE P18.18 million which, COA said, should have gone to legitimate beneficiaries.

It said: “In the absence of such documentation, the audit team could not sufficiently determine whether the beneficiaries were indeed medically fit to perform the assigned work or whether the contracted services were actually rendered.”

The concerned DOLE regional offices, in response to COA’s audit findings, agreed to strictly enforce beneficiary validation and verification procedures to ensure that only those who fully meet eligibility requirements are granted assistance.
Auditors also found 1,275 individuals in the Zamboanga Peninsula region were paid more than the amount they were meant to receive under the TUPAD program.
“Audit of disbursements of TUPAD showed that there were excessive payments to 1,275 beneficiaries totaling P6,463,150 due to lapses in the maintenance of the database,” the COA said.
In Soccskargen, in particular, 330 persons collected TUPAD assistance twice, 57 were paid three times, and 132 got the cash assistance four times, according to COA.

The multiple collection was attributed to “inadvertent” inclusion of certain beneficiaries to the TUPAD Program which was traced to submission of different lists or inconsistencies in the identification details.
State auditors recommended that the COA regional offices implement measures to recover the excess payments. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Romualdez's lead physician: No emergency, invasive procedure set for ex-Speaker
articles.summary: Dr. Rosalio Torres, the overall coordinator of the medical team of Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez, said Friday that the former House Speaker does not have any scheduled surgery or invasive…

blocks.text: Published September 11, 2026 11:10am

Dr. Rosalio Torres, the overall coordinator of the medical team of Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez, said Friday that the former House Speaker does not have any scheduled surgery or invasive medical procedure.
Torres made the testimony during Day 2 of the hearing on Romualdez's motion seeking hospital detention amid a P7.4 billion plunder case leveled against him over alleged links to flood control mess.
"None at the moment," Torres said when asked by the prosecution panel if there is any immediate surgery or invasive medical procedure scheduled to be done on Romualdez.
But when asked to confirm if there is no serious threat to the life of Romualdez that needs immediate intervention, Torres disagreed.
"I do not agree with the statement, based on the evaluation and recommendation as discussed with my consulting specialists, cardiologist, neurologist, and psychologist," Torres said.

Dr. Rody Sy, cardiologist of Romualdez, also testified that the lawmaker would need to be brought to a "hospital with angiographic facilities within one hour" in the event that the lawmaker suffers a heart attack.

Also on Friday, Dr. Kurt Sibayan, the admitting physician of Cardinal Santos Medical Center, clarified that he did not need to conduct an examination on Romualdez since his attending physicians were already there.
Sibayan made the clarification a day after he testified in court that the attending physicians of Romualdez advised them that they were not allowed inside the patient's room.
"The attending physicians are already there. It wasn't necessary for me to be there [to examine him]," Sibayan said during the questioning of Romualdez's counsel, Judd Roy III.
Asked by Roy if he was ordered to stay away, Sibayan replied "No."

It was Sibayan who prepared the clinical abstract of Romualdez, which was done by 8:15 p.m. of September 7, the same day that the Sandiganbayan ordered the arrest of the lawmaker and his three other co-accused.

Sibayan also told the anti-graft court that his medical abstract on Romualdez was verified by the attending physicians of Romualdez, namely cardiologist Dr. Rody Sy, hematologist Dr. Rosalio Torres, and neurologist Dr.Rogelio Libarres, as well as hospitalist identified by Sibayan as Dr. Kevin Yahot.
Sandiganbayan Associate Justice Ronald Moreno pointed out that Dr. Torres did not sign the medical abstract and raised doubt on whether Sibayan should be believed.
Sibayan responded by saying that the justices can ask Romualdez's attending physicians for clarification.
Romualdez was arrested while confined at Cardinal Santos Medical Center on September 7.
The Sandiganbayan Third Division already issued an order setting Romualdez's detention at the New Quezon City jail in Payatas. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Spanish lawmakers back citizenship for Sahrawis
articles.summary: Spanish lawmakers approved a bill that could give citizenship to tens of thousands of Sahrawis and their descendants, amid tense ties with Morocco. The legislation must now pass the senate.

image.caption: Tesh Sidi, the first woman of Sahrawi origin to serve in Spanish parliament, called for the adoption of the legislationImage: Susana Vera/REUTERS

blocks.text: Spanish lawmakers on Thursday voted to grant citizenship to people born in Western Sahara under Spanish colonization — a region now that is now largely controlled by Morocco.
The move could test Madrid's already delicate relations with Rabat, especially after the border crisis in Ceuta.
The lower house approved the bill by:

items: In favor: 168
Against: 31
Abstentions: 145

blocks.text: The legislation would grant Spanish nationality to Sahrawis born before September 29, 1977, and allow their descendants to obtain citizenship through naturalization.
Estimates of those eligible range from around 70,000 to more than 100,000.
The legislation must now pass the senate to become law.

blocks.caption: Many Sahrawis live in refugee camps in Tindouf, Algeria, or elsewhere abroad [FILE: February 25, 2025]Image: Juan Carlos Rojas/picture alliance

blocks.text: Morocco claims sovereignty over Western Sahara
Spain's ruling Socialist Party and its left-wing coalition partner Sumar supported the measure, while the conservative People's Party abstained and far-right Vox opposed it.

Sumar lawmaker Tesh Sidi, the first woman of Sahrawi origin to serve in parliament, said the legislation restores the "Spanish national identity card to those Sahrawis who once held ​and from whom this state took it away."
Spain controlled Western Sahara until 1976. Morocco claims sovereignty over the territory, while an indigenous resistance group, the Polisario Front, seeks independence.

Morocco occupies almost all of the territory. Meanwhile, the Polisario Front across the border in the Algerian town of Tindouf, where tens of thousands of displaced Saharawi people live in refugee camps.
The region remains on the United Nations' list of non-self-governing territories.
How the Ceuta influx raised tensions
The vote comes amid renewed tensions between Madrid and Rabat following a large influx of migrants into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta in July.
Scores of migrants died in their attempt to reach EU territory, most by drowning.
Western Sahara dispute: Morocco's gamble won global support
Although most of those who breached Ceuta's borders have returned, thousands remain, many of them unaccompanied minors living in dire conditions.
The incident caused a major rift among EU member states, most publicly between Spain's left-wing government and Italy's far-right leadership.

articles.title: New York marks 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks
articles.summary: NEW York, United States – New York commemorates the 25th anniversary of the devastating September 11, 2001 attacks Friday with a ceremony marked by US President Donald Trump’s absence and…

blocks.text: NEW York, United States – New York commemorates the 25th anniversary of the devastating September 11, 2001 attacks Friday with a ceremony marked by US President Donald Trump’s absence and right-wing outrage at the attendance of the city’s first Muslim mayor.
Trump will pay his respects at the Pentagon, not New York, where hijacked planes destroyed the World Trade Center and killed most of the 2,977 total victims on that world-altering day.

Vice President JD Vance and Trump’s four living predecessors – Republican George W. Bush, who was in office during the attacks, and Democrats Joe Biden, Barack Obama and Bill Clinton – are all expected at the “Ground Zero” site in lower Manhattan.
No one will give speeches at the ceremony, while bereaved family members will read out the names of all of those killed and a bell rung to mark major moments during the attack.

“Memorials like this and discussions about those events are an important part of keeping it alive and understanding how we prevent tragedies like this from ever happening again,” said Robert Kafka, a Chicagoan in his 60s visiting the 9/11 Memorial.

Alongside the former presidents will be Democratic Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the Big Apple’s first Muslim mayor, despite a campaign urging him to stay away spearheaded by the right-wing New York Post and former mayor Rudy Giuliani.

A petition, which has gathered more than 100,000 signatures, accuses Mamdani of associating with unspecified individuals who are “dismissive of American institutions or insufficiently critical of extremist ideologies.”
“It’s concerning to me that the mayor is being treated differently simply because he is Muslim,” city council member Shahana Hanif told CNN.
Mamdani won plaudits however for recently revealing thousands of documents showing what city officials knew about toxicity levels of the air in Lower Manhattan following the attacks.

After the initial dust cloud that followed the collapse of the World Trade Center, months of pollution and lingering dust ensued, causing cancers from which thousands of New Yorkers still suffer today.
Toxic air
“People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air,” Mamdani said Tuesday.
Nineteen Al-Qaeda operatives hijacked four planes on that nearly cloudless day in 2001. Two jets slammed into the World Trade Center’s Twin Towers, causing the iconic 110-story buildings to collapse.
A third plane struck the Pentagon, while a fourth crashed into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers fought back.
Beyond those killed on September 11, more than 9,400 other people have died from 9/11-related illnesses, according to the federal program established to provide medical care to those affected.
Some 100 million Americans were not even born or are too young to remember the tragic events.
Logan Miller, 32, lost his uncle during the attacks, and his grandfather to 9/11-related illness in the aftermath.
“I think the next generation just can’t fathom what actually transpired and how someone could be impacted by that, and so I actually find them asking more questions,” he told AFP.
Huge crowds are expected to gather in Lower Manhattan for the memorial service.
The Secret Service has erected a security ring of steel around the site of the 9/11 Memorial and Museum.
Police commissioner Jessica Tisch said an anti-drone team would be deployed as a precaution, but stressed there was no intelligence of a specific threat to the gathering.
Al-Qaeda meanwhile has marked the anniversary by releasing a video showing images of late leader Osama bin Laden and his son Hamza, who Trump said in 2019 had also been killed.
Ahead of the memorial, a drone show with 2,977 lights rose above New York Harbor, one for each person killed in the attacks./dp

articles.title: [The Wide Shot] The test that only you can grade
articles.summary: A letter to my journalism students as we hold yet another online class

blocks.text: Dear Class,
Reminder: Please strive to be honest.

Honesty is the true test of a journalist. In online assessments where I cannot check if you are cheating or not, another type of assessment is at work. It is an assessment of character, a test that only you can grade.
I hope you excel.

If you pass the test of honesty, you will pass the test of life. If you don’t, you will have small wins now — but trust me, you are doomed to fail in the end. Strive to build your skills through honesty and hard work, and God will reward you with the fullness of life.

Please stay honest in our online quizzes. If you cheat, you win some points now. But eventually, you lose your moral fiber, disintegrate, and become a monster unrecognized even by your own parents. We have been discussing corrupt politicians in class. You will be like them — reviled by the nation, abhorred even by children. Corrupt politicians started by cheating in class.

Please also stay honest in our online writing exercises. I designed these writing exercises to help you practice for our major assessments. I also want to identify the students who need extra help, so that I can meet them where they are. It is useless to cheat in online writing exercises because I do not grade these articles for quality, only for effort. If you cheat in online exercises, you cheat only yourselves.
Please do not mistake good writing for good journalism.
A good journalist is not just a good writer. A good journalist is a truth-teller.
I hope you can see the big picture: Our ultimate goal is not to ensure that you excel in school assessments. Our ultimate goal is to help each of you become a good person.
Be good!
And if you failed this test of life today, there is always tomorrow. There is hope.
Paterno

Paterno R. Esmaquel II is a journalist specializing in religion and public life. A former Rappler reporter and news editor, he now writes for international Catholic news outlets, teaches journalism at the University of Santo Tomas, and runs a YouTube channel called The Religion Reporter.
The author originally posted this to Facebook on September 10, 2026.
