MANILA, Philippines – Quezon City Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 98 has deferred the arraignment of Vice President Sara Duterte for her grave threats case originally scheduled on Friday, September 11.
Duterte’s lawyer, Paul Lawrence Lim, said they filed a motion with the court that prompted the tribunal to defer the Vice President’s arraignment.

“Ito’y pinagbigyan ng korte at pinapa-comment niya, pinapa-submit niya ng comment ang DOJ (Department of Justice), prosecution within a certain period. Tapos maaari rin kami sumagot kung sakali na kailangan, and then saka niya dedesisyunan ito, ‘yong aming motion,” Lim told reporters outside the court.
“Ngayon, pansamantala habang ito’y pinag-iisipan pa niya ‘yong aming motion, hindi muna matutuloy ‘yong arraignment, so suspended muna,” he added.

(The court acknowledged our motion and asked the DOJ, the prosecution, to comment within a certain period. And we can reply to that if ever, and then the judge will decide on our motion. For now, while the court is deliberating on our motion, the arraignment has been deferred, suspended for the meantime.)
The Vice President showed up during her arraignment on Friday morning. Her spokesperson and lawyer, Paolo Panelo, confirmed her attendance ahead of her arrival.
Arraignment is the phase in criminal proceedings that happens after the arrest or surrender.

This is when the court reads the accused his/her case, and asks him/her either for a guilty or not-guilty plea. If the accused entered a guilty plea, then the case will immediately move to conviction, usually with a lower sentence. If not guilty, then the case moves to trial.
It’s unclear what type of motion the defense has filed with the court. Even the DOJ did not disclose the nature of the said motion.

“The DOJ respects the Court’s decision to defer the arraignment pending resolution of the motion filed by the defense. We will allow the judicial process to take its course. At this point, the prosecution will reserve further comment until the motion has been resolved,” DOJ spokesperson Raphael Martinez told reporters in a message.
“Beyond what has already been stated, we would rather not further characterize or discuss the contents of the pending motion. At least not yet,” he added.
But under Section 11 of the Revised Rules of Criminal Procedure, a party may seek a suspension of arraignment on the following grounds:

items: The accused appears to be suffering from an unsound mental condition that effectively renders him/her to fully understand his/her case.
There is a prejudicial question
A petition for review of the resolution is pending either with the DOJ or Office of the President

blocks.text: So far, the only pending petition sought by the Duterte camp is a petition for review filed with the Supreme Court.

“We confirm that the Vice President has filed a petition, followed by an amended petition for certiorari and prohibition with application for TRO and/or Writ of Preliminary Mandatory Injunction with the Supreme Court a few days ago. The amended petition challenges the DOJ and Quezon City Regional Trial Court’s jurisdiction to prosecute her as an incumbent impeachable officer,” Lim said on Thursday.

Duterte, who was once allied with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., was charged with grave threats by the Department of Justice in August, in relation to her alleged assassination threats against Marcos, his wife Liza, and cousin, former House speaker Martin Romualdez.

It was the National Bureau of Investigation which initiated the criminal proceedings against Duterte after her infamous midnight press conference on November 23, 2024. She told her supporters at that time not to worry about her safety, adding that she had already “talked to someone” who would assassinate Marcos and his family if she were killed.
The grave threats allegation also formed part of one of the articles of impeachment in Duterte’s Senate impeachment trial.

On September 4, the Quezon City RTC Branch 98 ordered Duterte’s arrest after it found that there was probable cause – or enough evidence – to believe that the Vice President committed the crime. Duterte posted bail the following day, where she dropped her now-controversial line about “not feeling safe.”

“I do not feel safe. I do not feel safe anywhere. Pumunta lang ako [rito] kasi sabi ninyo pupunta ako sa court (I only went here because you told me I needed to appear in court),” Duterte said on Saturday, September 5.

blocks.caption: The meltdown of Sara Duterte: From ‘no joke, no joke’ to ‘I do not feel safe’

blocks.text: Before the court issued the warrant, Duterte’s camp had filed a motion to defer it. They had sought oral hearings as they they argued that Duterte cannot face a criminal case because she is an impeachable official.
But the court denied the motion to defer and proceeded to order Duterte’s arrest. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Hastie accepts apology from Joyce over ‘traitor’ cartoon as Hanson doubles down and tells critics to ‘chill’
articles.summary:
A split emerges in One Nation over the video, with Barnaby Joyce offering an apology as Pauline Hanson continues to refuse to take down the video

Andrew Hastie has accepted an apology from…

blocks.text: Andrew Hastie has accepted an apology from his former colleague Barnaby Joyce over a One Nation cartoon video labelling the former SAS captain a traitor but reiterated that he believed Pauline Hanson was a “lying coward”.

The apology has revealed a split between Joyce and his leader, as Hanson instead appeared to double down on the controversial animation on social media, thanking Hastie for drawing attention to the video posted more than one month ago and saying critics should “take a chill pill”.

Hastie had called on Hanson and One Nation to take ownership of the cartoon or remove it from social media, after the One Nation leader said she personally had not called the Liberal frontbencher a traitor.
The One Nation video posted to social media in late July depicts Hastie as a pitiful and paranoid opposition leader manipulated by Anthony Albanese into taking on One Nation.
It also refers to him being a traitor after he gave evidence against the Victoria Cross-winner Ben Roberts-Smith in his failed defamation trial.
Joyce quickly distanced himself from the video on Wednesday, saying he was not aware it. He later told the press he had reached out to Hastie.
On Friday Hastie told Guardian Australia he accepted Joyce’s explanation.
“Barnaby Joyce has reached out to me and explained that he didn’t know about the cartoon that called me a traitor eight times,” Hastie said. “I accept his explanation.
“I called him a lying coward because I thought he was protecting Pauline Hanson. I now know that she is the only lying coward.”
Hastie has accused Hanson of being “weak” and having a “glass jaw” and said the video not only insults him but all veterans, including others who gave evidence at the defamation trial.
Hanson has refused to apologise or pull down the video and has taken aim at critics including Jacqui Lambie, who backed Hastie and called the One Nation leader an “angry little woman”.
She posted a photo of Lambie on X and wrote: “I think everyone needs to take a chill pill.” The video remained pinned to the top of her X account on Friday.
Joyce would not weigh into whether the video should be taken down, telling News24 on Thursday night it was “beyond my pay grade”.
“I’m not responsible for putting the cartoons up and I’m not responsible for taking them down,” he MP said. “So, you know, it’s an odd discussion for me.

“If I believe a person’s hurt and I listen to it and I think, no, that’s fair enough, you’re not a traitor, therefore if you feel hurt by that because you think it’s too close to the bone, even though it’s a cartoon, I’m not making excuses because it’s a cartoon, but it wasn’t actually said by anybody in One Nation to him then nonetheless, it should be apologised for, so I apologise.”
But the One Nation senator Sean Bell said it was a “shame” Hastie had decided to make the issue about himself.

“I don’t think the party has anything to apologise for,” he told News24. “I think people should go and watch the cartoon, because I think, in it, there’s a lot of very insightful things, because it’s not just about Mr Hastie, it’s about the Liberal party as a whole. It’s about the Labor party and some of the tricks they use.
“Mr Hastie’s has been looking to have a fight and a conflict with One Nation for a long, long time.”
Senior Liberals, Lambie, the RSL and the Greens have all criticised the video, and pushed for it to be taken down.
On Friday the defence minister and deputy prime minister, Richard Marles, said the use of the word traitor was “tasteless”.

“Andrew Hastie is definitely not a traitor,” he told ABC radio. “I know him well and I’ve said this publicly. I very much honour the service that Andrew Hastie has given to our country, wearing our nation’s uniform. I think to use that word in respect of a veteran is extremely tasteless.
“No one should be using that word in respect of any veteran and in respect of Andrew.”

articles.title: More Tiananmen vigil activists sentenced to prison in Hong Kong security case
articles.summary: A Hong Kong court sentenced three activists — who for years organized vigils in remembrance of China's 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown — to prison for terms ranging from five to more than seven years…

image.caption: Lee Cheuk-yan, middle, and Albert Ho, far right, along with Chow Hang-tung were sentenced in a Hong Kong court Friday. (Tyrone Siu/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

A Hong Kong court sentenced three activists — who for years organized vigils in remembrance of China's 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown — to prison for terms ranging from five to more than seven years on Friday in a case that is widely seen as a barometer of the city's freedoms as Beijing clamps down on dissent.
The 3 activists were convicted under a Beijing-imposed national security law
Lee Cheuk-yan, Chow Hang-tung and Albert Ho were convicted of inciting subversion earlier this year under a Beijing-imposed national security law.

Lee and Chow, who pleaded not guilty, received prison terms of seven years, and seven years plus three months. Ho was given five years plus two months, lower than his co-defendants partly because of his guilty plea.
The trio of defendants was charged in September 2021 and has been held in custody for years.
Hong Kong once had a vibrant civil society marked by massive protests and a freewheeling press scene.

For three decades, the vigil was the only large-scale, public commemoration in China that drew tens of thousands of people annually. It symbolized the civil liberties Hong Kong enjoyed under Beijing's "one country, two systems" governing principle after Britain handed the former colony back to China in 1997.

items: Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty in 2nd national security case
Tiananmen Square vigil organizers convicted of 'inciting subversion' in Hong Kong

blocks.text: But after a 2019 protest movement rocked the city, authorities reduced public choice in elections and prosecuted leaders of news outlets known for their critical reports of the government. Many leading activists were imprisoned under the security law, and dozens of civil society groups dissolved, including the alliance.
Beijing says the law is necessary to maintain stability.
The sentences for the Tiananmen activists are the latest high-profile penalties imposed under the security law.
In February, former pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai was sentenced to 20 years in prison.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: News of 39 soldiers held by MILF is from 2023, not recent
articles.summary: The viral Facebook post was likely referring to a 2023 incident in Lanao del Sur that has been falsely presented as a recent development ahead of the BARMM polls on September 14

blocks.text: Claim: Members of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) blocked 39 soldiers from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and confiscated their firearms in Lanao del Sur on September 9.

Why we fact-checked this: A September 9 Facebook post published by the page “Kakatoh Trending” claims: “Breaking news! Hinarang ng MILF ang 39 na sundalo ng AFP na dumaan sa kanilang kampo sa Lanao del Sur at pinadeposito pa ang kanilang mga baril, ano ito? Bawian na sila?”
(Breaking news! The MILF intercepted 39 AFP soldiers passing through their camp in Lanao del Sur and even forced them to surrender their firearms, what is this? Is this a case of getting even?)
As of writing, the post has garnered over 859 reactions, 281 comments, and 70 shares. The page itself has more than 21,000 followers.
The post received several comments, most of which backed up the claim, with one comment adding, “Nakita ko na sa balita totoo ‘yan (I already saw that in the news, that is true).”
Another post uploaded on September 9 features an excerpt of a news report regarding the incident. As of writing, it has 7,800 reactions, 528 comments, 874 shares, and 314,000 views.
The posts began spreading ahead of the first-ever Bangsomoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections on September 14.

The facts: The false claim is likely referring to a real incident in February 2023, when 39 soldiers belonging to the 1st Special Forces Battalion were held and later released by the MILF after they strayed close to the Front’s 103 Base Camp in Barangay Delimbayan in Maguing town, Lanao del Sur.

The accounts that posted the false claim have been reposting the GMA News report of the incident without saying that it is a 2023 report. The post by the page “Kakatoh Trending” added a “breaking news” label, falsely implying that the incident happened recently.

According to Rappler’s 2023 report, officials said the incident stemmed from a lack of coordination between the Army’s Special Forces and the MILF — though the MILF claimed the soldiers in custody were only “requested” to surrender their firearms rather than being “disarmed.” The soldiers were later released following negotiations.

Commander Bravo’s “off-limits declaration”: The false claims began spreading after MILF leader Abdullah “Commander Bravo” Macapaar declared MILF communities in Lanao del Sur and Lanao del Norte as “off-limits” to government forces. His statement came after a large MILF convoy was intercepted on September 2 by soldiers and police in Lanao del Norte due to concerns over travel coordination.
These genuine media reports only mention an off-limits declaration, but do not confirm any actual blocking or disarming of soldiers.

In a September 9 Facebook post debunking Kakatoh Trending’s Facebook post, election monitor Independent Election Monitoring Center (IEMC) – BARMM said that following its initial checks with local military contacts, there was “no indication of a blockade, confrontation, or confiscation of firearms involving AFP and MILF personnel in Lanao del Sur.”

The IEMC – BARMM is a coalition of watchdog groups, including the Institute of Autonomy and Governance, National Citizens’ Movement for Free Elections, and Parish Pastoral Council Responsible for Voting, accredited by the Commission on Elections to monitor the BARMM polls.

BARMM parliamentary elections: The upcoming polls represent the Bangsamoro’s third attempt at establishing regional governance, following four postponements from the original 2022 election schedule through March 2026.

The BARMM’s parliamentary elections serve as a milestone in the region’s decades-long journey to peace following the MILF and the Philippine government’s historic peace agreement in 2014. The elections come amid persistence of violence and heightened security concerns, with 108 areas classified as election areas of concern, particularly in Lanao del Sur. (LIVE UPDATES: First BARMM parliamentary elections)

Debunked: In its post debunking the false claim, the IEMC – BARMM also warned against claims involving AFP–MILF security coordination, since unverified reports about such movements or security incidents can heighten tensions.
Rappler has previously debunked claims related to the BARMM and its upcoming elections:

items: FACT CHECK: No Turkish police deployed to secure BARMM polls
FACT CHECK: BARMM official’s ‘hate quote’ after MSU bombing is fake
FACT CHECK: No reports of MNLF, MILF plot vs Marcos gov’t over Duterte arrest

blocks.text: – John Jerome Santos/Rappler.com
John Jerome Santos is a research and data volunteer writer at Rappler. He is a fourth year Bachelor of Science in Accountancy student at the Dr. Gloria Lacson Foundation Colleges of Cabanatuan City.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Man flees road rage incident near Vancouver that ended with him being chased with a knife
articles.summary: Robin Nuber was in Los Angeles on the weekend, but it was after he returned home to British Columbia that he found himself in a scene he likened to an "action movie," speeding in reverse to escape a…

image.caption: Robin Nuber can be heard telling the man who was fleeing to 'hold on' to his car as he distanced it from the man with a knife. (Submitted by Robin Nuber)

blocks.text: British Columbia

Robin Nuber was in Los Angeles on the weekend, but it was after he returned home to British Columbia that he found himself in a scene he likened to an "action movie," speeding in reverse to escape a man with a knife who was chasing a frightened victim clinging to the outside of Nuber's Tesla.
Victim sustained multiple injuries, including cuts, a bloody mouth and a gouged-eye, says witness

"I just got back, so I literally felt like I was at Universal Studios where they do the staged remakes of movies, and everything's kind of like an action movie," the Surrey, B.C., photographer said on Thursday
"It felt like I was at an actual movie set, but nope, it was not — it was very real."

Nuber had been heading to a photo shoot in Redwood Park in Surrey on Wednesday when he encountered the scene of a man with a knife clambering over a pickup truck in pursuit of another man, who ran toward Nuber's Tesla.
A video captured by Nuber's vehicle shows the assailant chasing the car as it reverses away, the other man hanging onto an open back door as Nuber tries to put distance between them and the pursuer.
Nuber can be heard telling the victim to "hold on" before the vehicle stops and the man climbs inside when they are far enough away from the attacker.
He said the victim suffered multiple injuries, including a bloody mouth, gouged right eye and cuts on an arm.
Surrey police said a 37-year-old man was facing multiple charges, including assault with a weapon, criminal harassment and uttering threats and he remained in custody.
He was due in Surrey Provincial Court on Thursday to set a next appearance date.
"The victim attempted to drive away in his Ford pickup truck when the suspect drove his Jeep Wrangler into it," Surrey police said in a statement on Thursday.

"The victim then ran from the truck as the suspect allegedly brandished a knife and chased after him. Fortunately, a nearby witness driving a Telsa provided the victim safety until SPS officers arrived.

items: Cat in the Hat suspect who chased a teen girl in B.C. appears to be a trend copycat
North Vancouver road rage dispute over merging leaves 1 in critical condition: police

blocks.text: The statement said several police officers were called to the scene at about 4:44 p.m. and took the suspect into custody without incident.
Nuber said he had turned up at a parking lot when he saw a pickup truck and a Jeep had collided, with both cars' airbags deployed.
"I thought that it might be a road rage incident. So, I slowed my car down, and then I took my phone out and started to film what started to happen," said Nuber.
Then he heard someone yelling "he's got a knife.'
The chase ensued after a man with no shoes ran toward him, shouting for help.
"The guy basically ended up hanging onto my car and then being kind of dangled underneath the door for about 100 feet. I think I dragged him just to get him away from the guy," Nuber said.
"And then eventually he kind of begged me to stop the car so he could get inside because he was obviously getting road rash."
Nuber said the suspect gave up the chase, walked to the woods and threw the knife into the forest, before police arrived minutes later.
He said the incident was a test of his survival instincts.
"I think if you ever face a situation, you might be impressed with yourself, with what your instincts do," said Nuber.

articles.title: QC court defers Sara Duterte's arraignment as VP calls Marcos an 'addict'
articles.summary: The Quezon City Regional Trial Court deferred on Friday, September 11, the arraignment of Vice President Sara Duterte for her grave threats charge after a motion filed by her camp.

blocks.text: September 11, 2026 | 10:44am
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte (C) talks to her supporters after posting bail at a court building in Quezon City suburban Manila on September 5, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — The Quezon City Regional Trial Court deferred on Friday, September 11, the arraignment of Vice President Sara Duterte for her grave threats charge after a motion filed by her camp.
The court ordered the Department of Justice (DOJ) to comment on the motion before it rules, Duterte's lawyer Paul Lawrence Lim told reporters.
Until then, Duterte will not be formally read the charges or asked to enter a plea.
Duterte's lawyer declined to disclose the contents of the motion.
The DOJ, in a statement, said it respects the court's decision to postpone the arraignment pending a resolution of the motion by the defense.
"We will allow the judicial process to take its course. At this point, the prosecution will reserve further comment until the motion has been resolved," it said.
The department declined to comment on the nature of Duterte's motion.
Duterte went to the Quezon City Regional Trial Court in person on Friday, where she fired up a crowd of supporters in her calls for President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to step down.
"Umalis ka diyan! Sinungaling ka! Abusado ka!" she said, addressing Marcos. (Get out of there! You're a liar! You're abusive!)
She accused Marcos of bringing "nothing but hardship" to Filipinos and called him an "addict," a familiar refrain that her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, also hurled at Marcos.
"That's how it is with addicts. Their thinking is no longer grounded in reality," she said in Filipino.
"Remember, we will keep calling for the departure of our country's problem, whose name is Bongbong Marcos," she said.
Duterte thanked the crowd for skipping work "just to show the whole world the abusive nature of the administration."
"Our fight is not on social media, because our enemy is inside government buildings," she said.

The case against Duterte stems from a November 2024 briefing, where she said she had hired someone to kill Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez if she herself were killed.
The charges were filed in relation to Republic Act 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act.
The DOJ filed the case on August 11.
On September 4, a Quezon City court found probable cause to try Duterte, ordered her arrest and set bail at P120,000 per count.
Duterte appeared before the court and posted P360,000 in cash bail on September 5.
Duterte's lawyers argue that the trial court has no jurisdiction over the case, saying the 1987 Constitution gives impeachable officials limited procedural immunity while in office.
The Quezon City court already rejected her bid to quash the charges on jurisdictional grounds before it issued the arrest warrant.
In her petition before the Supreme Court, Duterte argued that prosecuting her while she is vice president is an illegal way of removing her from office without an impeachment conviction.

articles.title: Former Carlton president apologises to ex-wife as lewd photo defamation case settles
articles.summary:
Luke Sayers says he accepts Cate Sayers did not post photo of his genitals as she says settlement closes ‘painful and difficult chapter’

Embattled former AFL club president Luke Sayers has…

blocks.text: The embattled former AFL club president Luke Sayers has apologised to his former wife for the harm he caused as her defamation case over a lewd photo settled.
Lawyers for Sayers, the immediate past president of the Carlton football club, read out the apology in the Victorian supreme court on Friday after indicating the settlement.
“I acknowledge the extreme hurt and harm caused to Cate Sayers by suggesting she posted or may have posted [the lewd photo],” the barrister Sandip Mukerjea said on behalf of Sayers.
“I accept she did not do this. To the extent I may have suggested otherwise, I apologise unreservedly to her.”

Cate Sayers had claimed Luke Sayers had defamed her in a statutory declaration, which accused her of accessing his X account, posting a photograph of his genitals in January 2025 and tagging a female executive at Bupa.
The document was sworn by Luke Sayers in the weeks after the controversial post, which was quickly deleted, as the AFL and Carlton conducted investigations.
In May, Luke Sayers, a former PwC chief executive, applied to have the case transferred to the federal circuit and family court of Australia where the matter would be heard in private.
But Justice Andrew Watson rejected the application in June, finding the supreme court was the more appropriate venue for a defamation claim.
The judge on Friday dismissed the proceedings and commended the parties for reaching the settlement, the terms of which were not discussed in open court.
“All litigation involves time, expense and risk,” Watson said. “There was every reason to expect this proceeding would be no different.”
Outside court, Cate Sayers said she accepted her ex-husband’s apology and the settlement closed a “painful and difficult chapter” for her.
“I commenced these proceedings to establish the truth, clearly and finally,” she told reporters. “With Luke’s apology, I feel I have achieved what I set out to do.”
She thanked the women who had supported her and said she hoped Friday’s outcome gave them the strength to stand up for the truth.
She added that said she wanted to move forward with her life and did not confirm whether the settlement included a monetary component.
Luke Sayers chaired the Carlton board from 2021 to 2025. Before that, he headed consultancy firm PwC Australia between 2012 and 2020.
At an inquiry into a confidentiality and tax scandal in 2023, he apologised while stating he had no knowledge of it during his tenure.
“If the [tax office] had directly and formally advised me as the CEO of PwC Australia ... I would have sought details and ensured a full and thorough investigation,” he said at the time.

articles.title: Molly Ticehurst’s killer Daniel Billings sentenced to 28 years in jail for her murder
articles.summary: Ticehurst’s former partner had pleaded guilty to stabbing her 15 times at her Forbes home just before midnight on 21 April 2024

blocks.text: Molly Ticehurst’s ex-boyfriend has been sentenced to 28 years in jail for her senseless and brutal murder, which was revenge for her reporting allegations of sexual assault to police.
Daniel Billings was sentenced in the NSW supreme court in Orange today by Justice Natalie Adams, who imposed a non-parole period of 20 years.
Billings stood calm and expressionless when the sentence was handed down on Friday morning.
Ticehurst, a 28-year-old childcare worker, was found dead in her pyjamas at her home at Forbes, in the state’s central west, in the early hours of 22 April 2024.
Billings, her former boyfriend, broke into her bedroom and used a hunting knife to stab her 15 times in a ferocious attack that lasted less than a minute.
Adams found Billings’ offending was in the high range of seriousness, given he murdered her in the exact way he had long threatened to do.
“It must have been absolutely terrifying for Ms Ticehurst to die knowing her worst fears were realised,” Adams said.

The 31-year-old former mine worker had repeatedly threatened to smash into Ticehurst’s bedroom and kill her in the months after she ended their on-and-off relationship in December 2023, according to police documents.
Ticehurst reported this abuse to the police, who charged him with several counts of sexual assault and a series of domestic violence stalking and intimidation charges.
He was also charged with killing Ticehurst’s dachshund puppy with a hammer after an earlier break-up.
Police took out a provisional apprehended violence order against Billings, barring him from entering Forbes.

Billings, who previously lived in Dalby, Queensland, spent one night in police custody but was freed on bail by a local court registrar a fortnight before the murder as there was no judge on duty that weekend.
Upon his conditional release, Billings became enraged and obsessed with a belief he had been wrongfully accused of rape.
He viewed himself as a victim of injustice, also angered by his claim that police threw his Queensland State of Origin boxing team singlet in the dirt.
In a series of videos Billings recorded on his phone in the hours before the murder, he detailed his plans of harming Ticehurst in revenge.

“Molly Jean Ticehurst, well, you’ve done it, you’ve succeeded in whatever you wanted out of all of this, whether I get to you tonight or not,” Billings said in one of the recordings, made on the afternoon of 21 April.

Adams sentenced Billings to a maximum term of 28 years for what she described as a brutal attack. She found Billings acted out of retribution, revenge and “extreme hatred” for Ticehurst, angry after she reported the rape allegations.
after newsletter promotion
The murder was also a serious public justice offence, as Billings killed the only witness in his potential rape trial, the judge said.
Adams offered her condolences to the Ticehurst family. “It is clear that Molly’s senseless death has had a significant impact on those who loved her,” she said.
Gaby Shepherd held up a large image of her slain friend when Billings entered the courtroom and sat in the dock.
Billings did not look in her direction, instead staring straight ahead and shaking his head any time the sexual assault allegations were mentioned by the judge.
Prosecutors did not seek a life sentence for Billings.
Billings pleaded guilty to murder after more than 500 days of legal negotiations, which led to the sexual assault charges being dropped in November 2025.
Charges of property damage, the animal cruelty offence and breaching the apprehended violence order were taken into consideration in the sentence.

Ticehurst’s murder intensified a national campaign against domestic and gendered violence. The movement sparked changes to NSW laws, including stripping registrars of the power to grant bail, “show cause” thresholds for domestic violence-related bail applications and electronic monitoring for accused people.
Billings will be eligible for parole in April 2044.

articles.title: Texas reports first equine infection of New World screwworm on ranch horse
articles.summary:
The flesh-eating parasite had been largely eradicated, but now authorities are racing to contain an outbreak

A horse in southern Texas has been infected with the New World screwworm,…

blocks.text: A horse in southern Texas has been infected with the New World screwworm, marking the first US equine infection as health authorities race to contain an outbreak of the flesh-eating parasite.
The pest was discovered on the hind limb of a working ranch horse in Presidio county, according to a statement on Thursday from US Equestrian Foundation.
The foundation advised horse owners to monitor the animals daily for wounds, foul odor or maggots.
The screwworm, a fly larva, can nestle into and infest open wounds.

“Check horses daily, keep wounds clean and covered as directed by your veterinarian, use veterinarian-recommended fly control products and limit fly access with physical barriers such as fly masks, sheets and clean stabling practices when appropriate,” the foundation’s statement read.

The Texas Animal Health Commission, has restricted the movement of warm-blooded animals outside of infested zones in parts of Presidio and Jeff Davis counties, among several others, to curb new infestations.
After being eradicated decades ago, the screwworm was detected in June on a calf in Zavala county, near the US-Mexico border. A screwworm infestation has spread throughout Mexico.
Of the 49 US cases recorded this year, all have been in Texas, except for one in New Mexico, where the pest was found on a dog, according to the US Department of Agriculture.
The resurgence of the parasite, which can cause severe injury or death in animals, has raised alarm about potential financial devastation to Texas ranchers.
Greg Abbott, the Texas governor, issued a disaster proclamation in June to mobilize state resources toward coping with the rising screwworm presence.

Before the pest was reported on American soil, the Trump administration announced the launch of a sterile fly dispersal facility in Edinburg. If female screwworm flies mate with a sterile fly, their offspring will not be viable, thus curbing the population.
Reuters contributed reporting

articles.title: 'Nothing happens here. You're safe': 9/11 survivors, responders recall attack aftermath
articles.summary: Pilots, politicians, hotel workers, bus drivers and church leaders who had a front row seat to the aftermath of the Sept, 11, 2001, terrorist attacks gathered at the Gander airport on Thursday to…

image.caption: An evening of 'untold stories' from the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks was held at the Gander airport on Thursday night. Among those sharing their experiences were, from left, Gambo bus driver Frazer Lush, former federal transport minister David Collenette and Gander hospitality worker Lana Andre

blocks.text: Nfld. & Labrador·New

Pilots, politicians, hotel workers, bus drivers and church leaders who had a front row seat to the aftermath of the Sept, 11, 2001, terrorist attacks gathered at the Gander airport on Thursday to reflect on a life-changing experience.
Nearly 7,000 bewildered and scared passengers were stranded in Gander in the aftermath
David Collenette was addressing an audience in Montreal on the morning of Sept. 11, 2001.
At the time, the veteran Ontario politician was the federal minister of transport in the Liberal government of Jean Chrétien.
He began noticing some unusual rumblings in the audience, and then an aide walked up to him while he was speaking and presented him with a blunt note: "Wind up your speech. There's been a tragedy."
Passenger jets had been hijacked and were slamming into the World Trade Center towers in New York, the Pentagon in Washington, and a field in Pennsylvania.

As he scrambled back to Ottawa, Collenette was forced to make decisions that will forever be remembered in aviation history, including ordering 229 passenger jets bound for the United States to land immediately at Canadian airports, including those in Gander, St. John's, Stephenville and Happy Valley-Goose Bay.
Then, he ordered everyone to remain on the planes for hours until officials could be sure there were no more security threats.
"I think we made the right decisions," Collenette said during an event at Gander International Airport Thursday evening called "Untold Stories — Reconnected."

Hundreds of people gathered there to hear Collenette and others reflect on their experiences of the Sept. 11 attacks on the eve of the 25th anniversary of one of the most defining and catastrophic events in modern history. Just under 3,000 people were killed.

On that day, 38 commercial airliners touched down in Gander after North American airspace was closed in response to the attacks — delivering nearly 7,000 bewildered and scared passengers and crew to the central Newfoundland town, and effectively doubling Gander's population in a matter of hours.

The sudden arrival sparked a humanitarian response by area towns that inspired the hit musical Come From Away, and forged a unique and lasting bond between the stranded passengers and those who cared for them.

Thursday night's guest speakers included three of the pilots who landed their planes in Gander. One of them, Guy Gullick, was at the controls of US Airways Flight 3 from Rome to Philadelphia — the last plane to land in Gander that day.
'What kindness, compassion and humanity looks like'
After landing, Gullick wondered why there wasn't any security around the planes, an issue he raised when an airport employee boarded his jet.
Gullick said he'll never forget the answer to a very serious question: "He said, 'nothing happens here. You're safe."

It set the tone for the next several days, as passengers and air crews say they were treated to a level of hospitality and support that shocked and heartened those whose travel plans were upended by the attacks.
Gullick made special mention of hospitality worker Susan Scharpegge, who worked long hours and "slept on the floor" at the hotel "while we had rooms."
"You showed the world what kindness, compassion and humanity looks like," said Gullick. "You're an example for the world, and the world needs that right now."
Salvation Army officer Marlene George was among the responders and recalled encountering a worried and confused passenger.
George told the passenger that, "if you have to be stranded anywhere in the world, you landed in the right place."
She said area residents responded with "genuine love" to the so-called "plane people."
Striking school bus driver and Gambo resident, Frazer Lush, was among those who abandoned their picket lines to land a hand.
"It's not about a strike or a job. It's about helping people who needed us," said Lush, who also helped clean schools that had become emergency shelters.
Collenette, meanwhile, recalled the urgency he faced that day, with a plane entering Canadian airspace every 90 seconds and worries that one, or more, of them may pose a threat.
"We all had a job to do, and we reacted instinctively," he said. "Let's hope it doesn't happen again."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Terry Roberts is a reporter with CBC Newfoundland and Labrador, based in St. John’s. He previously worked for the Telegram, the Compass and the Northern Pen newspapers during a career that began in 1991. He can be reached by email at Terry.Roberts@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Sara Duterte expected to attend arraignment in grave threats case
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte is expected to attend her arraignment before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court on Friday, September 11.

blocks.text: September 11, 2026 | 8:29am

Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte (L) walks with one of her lawyers Paul Lim (R) as she arrives at a court building to post bail in Quezon City suburban Manila on September 5, 2026, after a warrant of arrest was issued. A Philippine court on September 4 issued an arrest warrant for Vice President Sara Duterte over an alleged death threat against the country's president, with her defence team saying she would "exercise all her legal remedies".
AFP / Ted Aljibe
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte is expected to attend her arraignment before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court on Friday, September 11.
Duterte is scheduled to appear at 8 a.m. Friday at the Quezon City Hall of Justice for her arraignment, her spokesperson lawyer Salvador Paolo Panelo Jr. confirmed on Thursday, September 10.

The vice president is facing three counts of grave threats over her remarks against President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
The charges stemmed from an online press briefing in November 2024, when Duterte said she had hired someone to kill the Marcos couple and Romualdez if she herself were killed.
The Quezon City court issued an arrest warrant against Duterte on September 4 after finding probable cause to hold her for trial. The warrant was served by police at the Office of the Vice President.
Duterte posted bail the following day at Quezon City RTC Branch 98, which was the assigned weekend court.
The court set bail at P120,000 for each count, or P360,000 in total. It later lifted the arrest warrant after Duterte's lawyers submitted the required documents.
During Friday's arraignment, the charges will be formally read to Duterte, after which she will be asked to enter a plea for each of the three counts.
If she pleads not guilty, the case will proceed toward trial and the court may set the next hearings.

Duterte's legal team has questioned the court's jurisdiction over the case. Her lawyers also argued that impeachable officials have limited procedural immunity while in office under the 1987 Constitution.
The court heard oral arguments on Duterte's motion to quash in late August.
The Department of Justice, however, maintained that there is prima facie evidence with reasonable certainty of conviction to support the three charges.
On Monday, Duterte's lawyers asked the Supreme Court to resolve her application for a temporary restraining order in the grave threats case before the Quezon City court.

The case is being heard as Duterte faces an impeachment trial before the Senate. The alleged threats against Marcos also form part of one of the Articles of Impeachment against the vice president. — with a report from Ian Laqui

articles.title: Trump’s Iran campaign echoes the post-9/11 ‘forever wars’
articles.summary: Critics say Trump has ignored key lessons from previous post-9/11 wars, including the risks of long-term engagements and the importance of international support, leading to a conflict that lacks…

items: Donald Trump's campaign for a second term promised to avoid foreign wars, yet he is now engaged in a conflict with Iran that analysts warn could become a prolonged 'forever war.'

The war against Iran is drawing comparisons to past conflicts in Iraq and Afghanistan, raising concerns about the lack of a clear exit strategy and the potential political repercussions for Trump's party in upcoming elections.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
WASHINGTON, USA – When Donald Trump campaigned for a second term in the White House, he promised to be a “president of peace” who would stop foreign wars, not start them.

Now, a quarter-century after the September 11, 2001, attacks that triggered America’s global “war on terror,” he is entangled in an unpopular conflict of his own making that analysts say risks becoming his version of a “forever war.”
With the 9/11 anniversary at hand, Trump’s war against Iran is drawing comparisons in foreign policy circles to the long, divisive conflicts in Afghanistan and Iraq that preceded it.
It is also prompting questions about whether the US has again failed to learn the lessons of past conflicts or prepare a clear exit strategy.

“Trump has broken an important post-Iraq and Afghanistan constraint in Washington against launching another major, open-ended war in the Middle East,” said Sina Toossi of the Center for International Policy, a Washington think tank. “That could leave his successor inheriting … an entrenched US-Iran confrontation.”

Administration officials have said the war against Iran is nothing like the protracted post-9/11 engagements.During the conflicts in Iraq and Afghanistan, the US removed hostile governments, committed thousands of ground troops who took and held territory, suffered and inflicted much higher casualties and struggled to instill Western-style governance.

This time, the US is relying mainly on air and naval power, operations that have damaged Iran militarily and economically but have not defeated it or spurred Iranians to overthrow their rulers as Trump initially urged.

But after six months of war, the United States is mired in a battle of attrition punctuated by bursts of hostilities – exemplified by this week’s exchange of attacks on oil tankers – while Trump tries to tighten the economic noose around Tehran.

Analysts warn it is likely to drag on well past the US midterm elections in November, when voters’ opposition to the war could threaten Trump’s Republican Party’s chances of keeping control of Congress.
And, much like those earlier conflicts, there is no obvious exit even as the economic costs weigh on US consumers.

Tehran’s disruption of oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed US gasoline prices higher. The war has weakened Trump’s approval ratings and undermined Washington’s international standing, which was also one of the repercussions from the Iraq and Afghan wars.

White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said Trump alone had “possessed the courage” to confront Iran over its nuclear program, that he had achieved all of his objectives and Iran’s economy was being crippled by stepped-up sanctions and a US maritime blockade.
She did not respond directly to Reuters’ questions on how the Iran conflict fits into America’s legacy of post-9/11 wars.

Analysts say Trump has failed to heed the central lessons of the post-9/11 era, which began after al Qaeda militants crashed planes into New York’s World Trade Center and the Pentagon outside Washington, killing nearly 3,000 people.
Those include the steep political downsides of long wars and the dangers posed by an entrenched foe fighting for its survival.

The attacks led to decades of conflict, starting with the invasion of Afghanistan, where al Qaeda leaders were sheltering, and followed by the 2003 invasion of Iraq, based on what turned out to be faulty intelligence that it was developing weapons of mass destruction.
The twin wars undertaken by President George W. Bush overstretched the US military and destabilized the Middle East.
The resulting US public backlash helped fuel Trump’s rise a decade ago, and he won a second term in 2024 vowing to avoid military adventurism and focus on Americans’ economic concerns.

But similar to how the Bush administration underestimated the insurgencies the US would face in Iraq and Afghanistan, Trump and his aides have miscalculated Iran’s resiliency and ability to throttle a fifth of the world’s energy shipments, analysts say.
Notably, Trump’s “Operation Epic Fury” launched alongside Israel on February 28 was not precipitated by a 9/11-type national trauma but was deemed by critics to be a war of choice.
Experts have disputed Trump’s claims that Tehran’s nuclear program posed an imminent threat to the US.

Iran may be taking a page from Afghanistan’s Taliban, who returned to power five years ago after a chaotic US withdrawal, that a determined foe can outlast Washington’s superior firepower while domestic pressure erodes its resolve.
The Iran conflict has also illustrated the cost of going to war with few allies on board.
Bush secured significant international support before launching his Iraq and Afghan campaigns, though that backing waned over time.
By contrast, Trump attacked Iran with little prior consultation or explanation and has found European and Asian leaders mostly resistant to his demands for assistance.

Relations with Trump had already been strained by his threat to seize Greenland, his questioning of NATO’s utility, his reduction of weapons supplies to Ukraine and his sweeping tariffs on trade partners.
The conflict has also mirrored the Iraq invasion in terms of a regional spillover that seemed to catch Washington off-guard, in this case Tehran’s retaliation against US Gulf allies.
With Iran’s neighbors quietly seeking to de-escalate a conflict they never wanted, a Gulf official lamented that the administration might be making some of the same errors of the post-9/11 wars.
“What was the (US) strategy here?” asked the official, speaking on condition of anonymity.
Saudi analyst Aziz Alghashian described “a sense of limitation and helplessness in the Gulf about the wars that are taking place due to the whims of the United States.”

The war’s shockwaves expanded on Thursday, September 10, with Yemeni government military sources saying Iran-aligned Houthis had seized control of the Yemeni port city of Mocha and gained further leverage over an important Red Sea oil-shipping route.
While the Iraq and Afghan wars ended as unpopular conflicts, both started with solid support at home.
Trump’s war enjoyed no such honeymoon in public opinion.
Most Americans were against it from the outset, and he has even drawn criticism from prominent figures associated with his “America First” movement.
Trump had initially expected to replicate his quick win from a January 3 raid that captured Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro.

But the Iran campaign instead has hardened into an uneasy stalemate that has not achieved most of Trump’s shifting objectives, including shutting down its nuclear program, and has depleted the Pentagon’s missile stockpiles.

Still, Trump is not without defenders.Mark Dubowitz, head of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a Washington think tank that takes a hard line against Iran’s rulers, denied Trump had plunged the US into an endless war and insisted he had scored successes that would eventually bring victory.
“It’s been a 47-year war waged by the Islamic Republic against America,” Dubowitz said. “And now we’ve struck back.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Reevaluating the latest re-rating upgrade of Megawide
articles.summary: Megawide offers investors a heavily de-risked, structurally protected entry into the most explosive infrastructure growth story in the market

blocks.text: From the latest company re-rating adjustment upgrades for Megawide Construction Corporation (trading symbol: MWIDE), the most aggressive was from First Metro Securities Brokerage Corporation (FirstMetroSec). It assigned a bold year-end “Take-Profit” (TP) target of P7.50 per share equivalent to a 57% upside from its trading close of P4.50 apiece on August 28 – a day before the issuance of the report.

The new upgrade coincides with another earlier company report of FirstMetroSec issued last year on September 15, 2025, wherein it first recommended buying Megawide with a 12-month target price of P4.50 per share. At the time, Megawide was trading within the price range of P2.70 apiece – an upside of 67%.

In the latest update, Megawide will more or less become what is called a double bagger (doubles your money by gaining a 100% return over your original purchase price) – or to be exact, 1.78% up – in the last two years if the oracles from FirstMetroSec turn out to be right.

FirstMetroSec pinned its conclusions not on Megawide’s capability as a pure brawn construction contractor in a tough industry but largely on a creative social infrastructure medium-term growth story (the 4PH housing program) that took roots from the “Double bottom line” and “3-D long-term strategic paradigm” of Edgar Saavedra’s blueprint for sustainable growth.

The 4PH program brings about a genuine structural shift. The 4PH program is not a typical real estate project: it’s a sizeable earnings platform, backed by a government policy that is anchored on a large housing backlog, supported by an affordable Pag-IBIG financing. Pag-IBIG is investing P10 billion via preferred shares to back the rollout of at least 7,000 affordable housing units over the near term, with an ultimate goal of developing 100,000 long-term units.

The partnership of Megawide with Pag-IBIG is a milestone that also directly addresses longstanding working capital strain problems. Like other players in the industry, Megawide suffers from erratic construction revenues and slow collections. The 4PH program changes that dynamic. It significantly reduces structural collection risks and improves working capital efficiency.

FirstMetroSec is also especially happy about the ongoing aggressive debt reduction program of Megawide that is scheduled to clear significant short-term obligations, drastically lowering financing costs and freeing up capital straight to the bottom line by 2027. This also includes the infusion of Citicore Holdings and Citicore Renewable Energy Corporation (CREC) monetization results to lower leverage. Net debt-gearing ratio is to decline to 0.8x by end-FY (Fiscal Year) 2027 from 1.40x in FY 2025. This gives Megawide room to scale 4PH without blowing up its debt load.

What’s more, Megawide is resuming its dividend policy. Megawide declared a P0.145 per share cash dividend and raised its dividend ceiling to 50% of prior-year income. Management plans to establish regular payouts starting in 2027.
Megawide’s market performance following the issuance of the upward re-rating report on August 31, 2026, experienced a notable upward trajectory, as shown in the details below:

On the first trading day on September 1 after the upgrade, Megawide’s stock price immediately leaped by 3.77% and reached an intra-day high of P5. By September 3, momentum pushed the stock to a closing high of P5.13, representing a 7.52% net gain within two days of the re-rating announcement.

From the profile of the market’s total value turnover above, it appears that the market play in Megawide is still largely confined to local investors’ punting. Foreign investors have yet to show any significant activity. Their highest participation is so far at 15% last September 4. Otherwise, their trading participation to total market transactions on the stock is still in single digits.

However, notice the movement of its stock’s price direction. When foreign investors’ transactions move higher in either direction, they have a commensurate impact. Megawide’s stock price dropped when foreign investors ended as net sellers like last September 2, while it rose when they ended as net buyers.

Another example is the trading result of Megawide’s stock price movement last September 8. Megawide’s stock price was foiled from going up any higher as foreign investors’ selling activities rose to 13.47% of total value turnover for the stock. And while foreign investors were net buyers last September 9, their volume was too negligible to make an impact on Megawide’s price direction.

Obviously, the immediate price resistance of Megawide is at P5.30. This matches its current 52-week high. Breaking past this level may take a while. Its price momentum seemed to have weakened as it faces strong resistance all the way to the psychological resistance markers of P5.50 and P6. But to ultimately break out from these levels may lead to an easy path towards the P7.50 target.

Even FirstMetroSec, as well as critics, also noted that there are potential risks in Megawide’s transition program like project delays, payment issues in affordable housing, and the concentration of future earnings to one project. But as Megawide’s performance record would show, it has strong management, partnerships, and advanced technology that could effectively render these risks into manageable obstacles.

For instance, although execution risks naturally accompany large-scale rollouts, Megawide owns a distinct competitive advantage through its proprietary advanced precast technology. This capability ensures unprecedented construction velocity, superior cost control, and rapid asset turnover, effectively isolating the company from the delays that typically plague standard contractors.

Furthermore, Megawide’s stellar operational history that includes the delivery of 10,000 public classrooms, major international airports, and the highly successful Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX), proves its capacity to execute major state infrastructure projects on time and at scale.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by Megawide (@officialmegawide)

It is also claimed that Megawide may become increasingly dependent on a single government program. This refers to its major participation in the 4PH program, which will contribute 36% of revenue by FY 2028. It is feared that any policy shift, budget constraint, or change in Pag-IBIG priorities could materially affect Megaweide’s performance. They say that if this happens, Megawide’s growth would stall.

The 4PH program is not a typical speculative government contract. Affordable housing is a top-tier national priority with massive, non-partisan political and social backing. The demand is structurally insulated from typical market cycles. Megawide is not just a contractor. It is a critical infrastructure partner. The sheer scale of the housing backlog ensures that no single political shift can abruptly halt the program without severe public backlash. Megawide can also leverage this massive pipeline to achieve economies of scale, lowering construction costs across its entire portfolio.

Moreover, Pag-IBIG is one of the most financially stable and liquid government-linked institutions in the country, funded continuously by mandatory member contributions. Pag-IBIG’s P10 billion preferred share investment in Megawide physically aligns their financial interests. Pag-IBIG is highly unlikely to change its priorities or restrict budgets when it is literally an equity stakeholder invested in Megawide’s success. This investment effectively locks in institutional commitment.

The traditional working capital constraints and collection uncertainties – which is not just Megawide’s problem but an industry constraint – are fully mitigated by a landmark institutional partnership with Pag-IBIG. This partnership completely front-loads the liquidity required to deliver the initial wave of housing units, eliminating development friction and insulating the company from cash conversion bottlenecks. Collections are directly tied to construction milestones and fully backed by subsidized Pag-IBIG-linked financing, ensuring a highly predictable cash conversion model that minimizes buyer back-out risks.

Financially, the company has completed its core balance sheet repair, erasing historical debt concerns through a P9.4 billion capital repositioning. Consequently, its net debt gearing ratio is projected to fall sharply from 1.40x in FY 2025 to just 0.8x by end-FY 2027, creating massive bottom-line expansion through reduced financing expenses.

Backed by an expanded 50% maximum cash dividend payout policy and a highly visible path to earnings expansion, Megawide offers investors a heavily de-risked, structurally protected entry into the most explosive infrastructure growth story in the market.

For forward-looking investors, therefore, Megawide provides an unmatched combination of policy-backed revenue visibility, aggressive deleveraging, and institutional validation that far outweighs any short-term macro caveats. – Rappler.com

articles.title: [Newsstand] ‘I don’t feel safe’ is Sara Duterte’s presidential campaign in a nutshell
articles.summary: It may have come across as simultaneously scripted and badly acted, but the Vice President’s melodramatic message has potent electoral appeal

blocks.text: Why the grave threats charges were only belatedly filed is another matter altogether, but Vice President Sara Duterte and her staff were fully prepared for them. Part of the preparation, self-evidently, was a narrative strategy.

According to Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla, Duterte’s representatives asked that she be detained in Camp Crime, the headquarters of the Philippine National Police. “Gusto niya na may picture siya na naka-handcuff. Gusto niya na may picture siyang nakakulong (She wanted to have a picture of herself in handcuffs. She wanted a picture of herself behind bars).”

Granted, this is Remulla speaking, one half of the sibling act which has been criticized for executing policy, or even policymaking, through press conferences. But the supposed conditions for Duterte’s surrender come straight from her father’s highly successful political playbook: When necessary, play the victim.

Also, the chief of the PNP’s Criminal Investigation and Detection Group, Police Major General Robert Norico II, said much the same thing. “I was informed by the [Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group] that she did not want to post bail. She wanted to be incarcerated.”

There was a change of mind, however, and the day after the arrest warrant was issued, the Vice President posted bail before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court. But she hesitated to enter the court’s premises for a long time. Talking to her lawyers while surrounded by the reporters, the photographers, and the cameramen who were covering the second highest official of the country as she made bail, she said she did not trust the court or the police. “I do not feel safe,” she said. “I do not feel safe anywhere.”

She said she was at the courthouse only because she needed to post bail on their advice (“sabi ninyo”). She said she wanted the media to accompany her inside. When told by her own lawyers that the media could enter only up to the staircase, following the court’s guidelines, she asked, in Filipino: “Who will be at my back? Do you remember Ninoy Aquino, he died on the stairs.”
Eventually she went in, posted a total of P360,000 in bail, submitted her own photos in lieu of the so-called mug shot, posed with supporters outside the courtroom, then left.

Sara Duterte is a woman of few words. Last July, on the second day of her impeachment trial, she showed up at the Senate to meet her lawyers and then issued a one-sentence statement: “In this bloodbath and bludgeoning, I will be bloodied but unbowed.”

When she posted bail some nine weeks after her impeachment trial started, she said considerably more than one sentence. But the core message, which she repeated often — sometimes like a bad line reading, sometimes like she truly meant it — was all of five words: “I do not feel safe.”
She said the threats she faced, from the police, among others, were “documented since 2023.” Then she returned to her theme and expanded it.

“I do not feel safe at all…kahit saan man. Hindi lang ako ‘yun, ha? Hindi lang ako ang ganito ang pakiramdam sa bansang ito, hindi lang ako…. ‘Yun ‘yung sentiment ko, ha? Hindi ito sa akin lang. Ang dami-dami nating mga kababayan ganoon yung pakiramdam nila. Hindi nila alam kung uuwi sila ma-hohold-up. Kada patak ng ulan hindi nila alam kung madadala yung bahay nila. Nobody feels safe in this country.”
It’s worth rendering the entire passage in English:

“I do not feel safe at all … anywhere. And it’s not just me. I’m not the only who feels this way about this country. I’m not the only one … That’s my sentiment. [But] It’s not mine alone. We have so many countrymen who feel this way. They don’t know if when they go home they will be held up. Every drop of rain, they don’t know if their house will be carried away [by a flood]. Nobody feels safe in this country.”
There is much that is hypocritical about this speechlet, or the core message itself.

First. When the vice president’s father, Rodrigo Duterte, ruled the Philippines with an iron fist and waged his so-called war on drugs, public opinion consistently showed both outright support for it and high levels of discomfort about it. Surveys showed that at the height of the so-called war, with thousands of extra-judicial killings already recorded, more than three-fourths of voting-age Filipinos said they were worried that they or someone they knew would be the next EJK victim. I called it “an extraordinary index of anxiety.”
Second. The vice president is also secured by a bodyguard numbering in the hundreds; she enjoyed their protection even on the day she posted bail.
Third. The large-scale corruption of flood control funds can also be traced back to the Duterte presidency.

But a theme does not need to be true to earn traction. And as we have learned from the very same playbook that the Marcos family used to rehabilitate its name and that the Duterte family applied to widen its appeal, a little truth wrapped around a big lie can carry it a long way.

The rampaging floods in the last few weeks drove many to anger; the external pressure on gas prices, on consumer goods, on the Philippine peso have stoked anxiety; the specter of violence reappearing in the Bangsamoro region, the reality of recurring power outages in the Visayas, the waste of previous classroom time because of inefficient or incoherent class suspension policies in the face of heavy rainfall — these have added to a sense of helplessness.

It would be easy for an ordinary citizen to sympathize with that five-word core message: “I do not feel safe.” This was the unspoken appeal of the EJKs; it seemed to eliminate those people on the street who made us feel unsafe. (But we have forgotten that this sense was not in fact a simple one: A large part of the public supported the campaign against illegal drugs, but was anxious about the killings.)
Soon after the vice president posted bail and articulated her “sentiment,” the phrase was picked up on social media.

Just one example: At 2.27 pm on Saturday, the vice president’s brother, Rep. Paolo Duterte, posted an arresting infographic on Facebook, with the following message on it: “I am with VP Inday. I am a Filipino. And I don’t feel safe.”

To their credit, some critics of the Dutertes have taken up the viral challenge and attempted to hijack the vice president’s theme. But there was no one common expression. The valiant attempts included: “I am a Filipino and I don’t feel safe with the Dutertes.” “I am a Filipino and I don’t feel safe with the Dutertes in power.” And: “I am a Filipino. I denounce the actions of VP Inday. At lalong hindi ako safe sa pamumuno ng mga Duterte.”
The counter-messaging (among many other factors) needs work. Simplest is best. – Rappler.com
Veteran journalist John Nery is a Rappler columnist. He anchors Rappler’s special coverage of the Duterte impeachment trial and hosts In the Public Square with John Nery every Wednesday.

articles.title: Cat in the Hat suspect who chased a teen girl in B.C. appears to be a trend copycat
articles.summary: A disturbing incident in which someone dressed in a Cat in the Hat costume chased a teenager in West Kelowna, B.C., occurred amid an online trend that twists the popular children's character into…

image.caption: B.C. RCMP spokesperson Staff Sgt. Kris Clark says police were already aware of the trend ahead of the Aug. 24, 2026, incident. (West Kelowna RCMP)

blocks.text: British Columbia

A disturbing incident in which someone dressed in a Cat in the Hat costume chased a teenager in West Kelowna, B.C., occurred amid an online trend that twists the popular children's character into something sinister, leading police in some jurisdictions to warn of offline consequences.
Police warn that threatening posts can have real consequences
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Sep 10, 2026 7:25 PM EDT | Last Updated: 10 minutes ago

While the incident in the Okanagan region last month happened in real life and has triggered an RCMP investigation, the Cat in the Hat social media trend typically involves generative AI depictions of the character and his distinctive red-and-white striped hat standing outside schools, homes or other locations.
Posts include TikTok videos with thousands of views showing the character in front of B.C. secondary schools or malls.
Other posts have included the names of individuals and their schools along with onscreen text such as "see you soon" or "bye bye."
With captions like "watch out," and "you're next," the unsettling images are leading police to warn the posts may have real world consequences if taken too far.

items: B.C. teen girl chased by Cat in the Hat amid online trend
RCMP say they arrested youth east of Ottawa because of potential threat

blocks.text: This week the Nechako Lakes school district in B.C.'s central Interior said it was aware of the social media trend and asked community members to report the posts to police.

B.C. RCMP spokesman Staff Sgt. Kris Clark said police were aware of the trend, including a case in Fort St. James in the Nechako Lakes school district, as well as the West Kelowna incident on Aug. 24 that was described by police on Tuesday.
Clark said he was "not aware of any other events in B.C. RCMP jurisdictions."
The criminality
Regarding criminality, "it would depend on the totality of the circumstances and whether sufficient evidence existed before an assessment for charge approval could be made," he said.

"Generally speaking, based on what I have seen, some potential offences could be uttering threats or criminal harassment; however, there are any number of others that may be considered depending on the available evidence."

West Kelowna RCMP had said last month's "concerning prank" may constitute criminal harassment, and other charges such as assault, uttering threats or intimidation could be considered if the evidence supported them.

"Regardless of whether the individual intended the behaviour as a joke, following a young person and causing them to fear for their safety is extremely concerning," Cpl. Devon Gerrits said in a statement, which included a photo of the character taken at night.
“People should understand that behaviour intended as a prank can have serious consequences when it causes another person to reasonably fear for their safety.”

Police in Tennessee, meanwhile, have said a student was arrested for making threats against school property with an AI-generated Cat in the Hat post and a teenager in Colorado was charged with harassment for a similar post that implied the character would appear outside a middle school and homes.

The Cat in the Hat character first appeared in the book of the same name by Theodor "Dr. Seuss" Geisel in 1957, but the costumed version from the videos is seemingly inspired by the 2003 live-action movie starring Canadian actor Mike Myers.
A viral post about the costume from the movie going up for auction may have sparked the horror-inspired trend, with some commenters describing it as uncanny and "nightmare fuel."

articles.title: Ukraine's fortress cities under fire as Russia bids to seize rest of Donbas
articles.summary: Kramatorsk and Slovyansk are now the main focus of Russian ground assaults, and residents are being told to leave.

blocks.text: It is so dangerous now in Slovyansk and Kramatorsk that police say it is time for civilians to get out. These neighbouring cities are the biggest still under full Ukrainian control in the eastern Donbas region.
In the worst affected areas, forced evacuations of families with children have already begun, says Pavlo Dyachenko of Donetsk police.
"This is the only way to save your life," he says, because security has deteriorated so much.
"If you take Slovyansk, it used to be hit by glide bombs roughly once a week, but now it's almost every day."
Slovyansk, Kramatorsk and Kostyantynivka, to the south, form part of what is known as Ukraine's "fortress belt" – a system of heavily reinforced defence lines in the east.
However, Kostyantynivka only has a limited presence of Ukrainian troops left, reports say, while Russia claims to be in full control of it.
Over the summer, the number of civilians wounded by Russian attacks on the two cities increased from 70 in June to 212 in August, say Ukrainian police.
Sixteen people died in June, 20 in July and 15 in August.
Residential housing comes under attack as well as infrastructure, says Dyachenko, causing "very significant destruction".
The number of glide bombs launched by Russia jumped from 40 in June to 109 in July and 92 in August, according to data published by Ukrainian police and studied by the BBC.
One morning two weeks ago, on 25 August, nine glide bombs targeted Kramatorsk. Seven hit civilian apartment blocks, wounding 24 people including a two-month-old baby, Ukrainian police say.
Two days later, it was hit again, this time with seven glide bombs, and five bombs targeted Slovyansk.
Fitted with winglets so they can glide to their target rather than fall, glide bombs are considered one of the most effective and lethal weapons in Russia's arsenal.
Usually, they weigh 250 or 500 kg, but there have been cases of Russia deploying bombs that weigh 1,500 kg.
"The devastation they cause is simply incredible," says Dyachenko.
"Glide bombs are the big fear," another British volunteer, John Auckland Abbey, posted on social media.

"They are silent killers, and when you've been abruptly woken by one exploding, you know at least another one will follow. The question you ask yourself as you lie very still in the dark is: will the next one be closer?"
Kramatorsk is currently home to the headquarters of the Donetsk regional administration. The capital city used to be Donetsk, until it was captured in 2014 by Russian-backed separatists.

What happens to the areas of Donbas still under Ukrainian control was reportedly a key issue when US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky last weekend after their talks with Putin.
In the past, Witkoff has appeared to back Russian claims to the region, but Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is refusing to pull troops out of it.
He says Putin has given his generals until the end of the year to complete their occupation of Donbas.
"Putin's primary objective on the front line remains the same: Kostyantynivka-Slovyansk," Zelensky told journalists last month.

Faced with mounting military pressure, the Ukrainian leader has created two new taskforces headed by experienced generals, Andriy Biletsky and Denys Prokopenko, to defend the portion of Donbas still in Ukrainian hands.
"There isn't just a battle for Donbas there," one unnamed Ukrainian general has said.
"What is probably the main battle of this year and the next is now unfolding."

image.caption: In an emailed statement Thursday, Ontario Public Service Employees Union (OPSEU) local 549 said that 27 permanent roles and four contract roles at the centre were affected by the layoffs. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto·New
In an emailed statement Thursday, Ontario Public Service Employees Union (OPSEU) Local 549 told CBC News that 27 permanent roles and four contract roles at the centre were impacted.
27 permanent roles, 4 contract roles impacted, union says
The Ontario Science Centre has laid off 31 workers, CBC News has learned.
In an emailed statement Thursday, Ontario Public Service Employees Union (OPSEU) Local 549 said 27 permanent roles and four contract roles at the centre were impacted.

Scott Clark, spokesperson for Ontario's Tourism Ministry, said the Ontario Science Centre is "making changes to effectively and successfully deliver science learning experiences" and programming at its interim Harbourfront Centre location and future Ontario Place location.
Those changes will create 1,000 new jobs, Clark said in an emailed statement Thursday, noting that there will be "no change" to programming and learning experiences delivered by the centre.
"New roles will be available for some of the impacted individuals at the interim and permanent [locations]," he said.

items: Ontario Science Centre to close immediately: province

blocks.text: The province abruptly closed the science centre in east Toronto in the summer of 2024, citing an engineering report that found deficiencies with the roof. Critics have questioned that reasoning given the roof has survived record snowfall and rainfall in the past two years.
The government is currently building a new $1-billion science centre at Ontario Place with the goal to open by 2029.

Philstar.com / Contributed photo
MANILA, Philippines — Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez will remain at Cardinal Santos Medical Center for now as the Sandiganbayan continues to hear his request to be confined at the hospital.
The Sandiganbayan Third Division said the status quo remains in effect because it has yet to finish hearing Romualdez’s motion for continued hospital confinement.
The hearing will resume on Friday, September 11, when Romualdez’s doctors are expected to return to explain his medical condition.

Cardinal Santos team manager Dr. Rosalio Torres told the court Thursday that Romualdez is at high risk of a possible heart attack. He said transferring Romualdez could compromise the “golden hour,” or the critical period after symptoms appear when medical intervention is needed to prevent serious heart damage or death.
The prosecution has opposed Romualdez’s request to remain at Cardinal Santos and asked the court to allow independent government doctors to assess his condition.
It also asked that Romualdez be detained at a facility of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP).

The Sandiganbayan earlier ordered the transfer of Romualdez’s custody from the Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group to the BJMP as he faces a P7.44-billion plunder charge over alleged kickbacks from government infrastructure projects.

The BJMP took custody of Romualdez at around 4:15 p.m. Thursday. His transfer to the New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas, however, has not yet been implemented while his hospital-confinement motion remains unresolved.
The BJMP said Romualdez would receive the same treatment and privileges as other persons deprived of liberty, with no VIP or special treatment.
The bureau has also prepared a detention cell at the Quezon City jail that can accommodate 10 people.
Romualdez was arrested on September 7 while confined at Cardinal Santos. The PNP said he remains medically unfit to travel based on a certification from the hospital.

During Thursday’s hearing, Cardinal Santos admitting physician Dr. Kurt Allen Sibayan said Romualdez’s admission was unusual because he was brought directly to his hospital room instead of the emergency room despite complaining of chest pain.
Sibayan also said he was not allowed to enter Romualdez’s room to examine him, which he said was not usual hospital practice.
Romualdez is accused of repeatedly receiving kickbacks and other pecuniary benefits from former lawmaker Zaldy Co on at least 15 occasions between 2022 and 2025, according to state prosecutors.
His arraignment and pretrial are scheduled for September 14. — with a report from Daphne Galvez
